methodologyNotes: Authored solely from the raw source text of doc-b (the Third Amendment and its Exhibit A blackline of the Amended and Restated Credit Agreement) plus the deterministic structural index; the base agreement text (doc-a) was consulted only as a second source document to locate which passages of Exhibit A differ from the 2022 original. Granularity follows the base-agreement convention: Article VI negative covenants are enumerated at lettered-basket (and, for Section 6.08, numbered-clause) level; Articles II-V and VII-XII are captured at section level; Article I is captured at defined-term level for financially operative, capacity-driving, entity-scoping and newly added or amended definitions, with narrow boilerplate definitions grouped into cluster units. Because Exhibit A restates the ENTIRE credit agreement, every unit records what the provision says AS AMENDED as of August 14, 2024, not merely that it was amended.

amendmentEffectivenessConditions.description: Section 4(a): the Administrative Agent must have received counterparts of the Amendment duly executed by (i) each Borrower and each other Loan Party, (ii) the Existing Required Lenders, (iii) each Third Amendment Incremental Lender and (iv) the Administrative Agent.

Section 4(b): the representations and warranties in Article III of the Existing Credit Agreement and the other Loan Documents must be true and correct in all material respects (in all respects for representations qualified by materiality or Material Adverse Effect), with specified-date representations tested as of that earlier date.
Section 4(c): no Default or Event of Default shall exist.

Section 4(d): the Company must be in compliance, on a pro forma basis after giving effect to the ENTIRE amount of the Third Amendment Incremental Term Loans and Third Amendment Incremental Revolving Commitments as if fully drawn or funded, with the covenants in Section 6.12 of the Existing Credit Agreement (including any applicable Total Net Leverage Ratio Adjustment).

Section 4(e): the Administrative Agent must have received a certificate dated the Third Amendment Effective Date from a Responsible Officer of the Company (on behalf of each Loan Party) certifying satisfaction of the conditions in Sections 4(b), 4(c) and 4(d).

Section 4(f): the Administrative Agent must have received (i) a secretary's or assistant secretary's certificate for each Loan Party certifying authorizing resolutions, incumbency and signatures, and attaching charter/organizational documents certified by the relevant authority and bylaws or operating/partnership agreements, and (ii) a good standing certificate for each Loan Party from its jurisdiction of organization.

Section 4(g): the Administrative Agent must have received a solvency certificate dated the Third Amendment Effective Date from the chief financial officer, chief accounting officer or other financial officer of the Company substantially in the form of Exhibit B to the Amendment.

Section 4(h): the Administrative Agent must have received a customary written opinion of the Loan Parties' U.S. and Canadian counsel, addressed to the Administrative Agent and the Lenders (including the Third Amendment Incremental Lenders) and dated the Third Amendment Effective Date, in form and substance reasonably satisfactory to the Administrative Agent.

Section 4(i): the Administrative Agent must have received a Borrowing Request in respect of the Third Amendment Incremental Term Loans no less than two Business Days prior to the Third Amendment Effective Date.

Section 4(j): with respect to the revolving increase, any fundings, repayments or reborrowings of Revolving Loans required by Section 2.09(g) of the Credit Agreement must be completed to reallocate outstanding Revolving Exposure after giving effect to the Third Amendment Incremental Revolving Commitments.

Section 4(k): all costs, fees and reasonable documented out-of-pocket expenses (including legal fees invoiced three Business Days, or such shorter period as agreed, before the Third Amendment Effective Date) and all other compensation payable to any Arranger or Lenders in connection with the Amendment must have been paid on or prior to the Third Amendment Effective Date (or authorized to be deducted from the proceeds of the initial funding of the Third Amendment Incremental Term Loans).

Section 4(l): the Third Amendment Incremental Lenders must have received, at least three days prior to the Third Amendment Effective Date (to the extent requested in writing at least ten days prior), (i) all KYC and anti-money laundering documentation including under the USA PATRIOT Act and (ii) to the extent the Borrowers qualify as a 'legal entity customer' under the Beneficial Ownership Regulation, a Beneficial Ownership Certification.

Structural condition (Section 3 lead-in): the New Lender joinders and the Third Amendment Incremental Term Loan and Revolving Commitments take effect 'substantially concurrently with' the effectiveness of the Section 2(b) amendments to the Existing Credit Agreement.

Sequencing condition (Section 2): the Section 2(a) consent to raise the Section 2.09(e) incremental cap from $200,000,000 to $255,000,000 takes effect IMMEDIATELY PRIOR TO the Section 2(b) restatement, and the Section 2(b) restatement (including the reset of the cap to $300,000,000 measured after the Third Amendment Effective Date) takes effect IMMEDIATELY AFTER Section 2(a).

articles.heading: Definitions (as amended and restated by Exhibit A)

units.description: 'Third Amendment' means the Third Amendment to Amended and Restated Credit Agreement dated as of the Third Amendment Effective Date among the Company, the other Loan Parties, the Lenders party thereto and the Administrative Agent. NEW definition added by this amendment.

'Third Amendment Effective Date' means August 14, 2024. NEW definition; it is the reference date for the reset incremental facility cap, the Total Net Leverage Ratio Adjustment usage counter, the restated aggregate Revolving Commitments and the new term loan tranche.
'Third Amendment Incremental Term Loan' means the term loans made pursuant to Section 2.01(e). NEW definition creating a new Class of Term Loans.

'Third Amendment Incremental Term Loan Commitment' means each Third Amendment Incremental Term Lender's commitment to make a Third Amendment Incremental Term Loan on the Third Amendment Effective Date in the amount set opposite its name on the Commitment Schedule; the aggregate amount of such commitments on the Third Amendment Effective Date (immediately prior to funding) is $200,000,000. NEW definition.
keyDefinedTerms: Third Amendment Incremental Term Loan Commitment

units.description: 'Third Amendment Incremental Term Loan Maturity Date' means April 1, 2027 (or the next succeeding Business Day). NEW definition - the new tranche is coterminous with the existing term facilities.
keyDefinedTerms: Third Amendment Incremental Term Loan Maturity Date

units.description: 'Third Amendment Incremental Term Lender' means a Lender with a Third Amendment Incremental Term Loan Commitment or an outstanding Third Amendment Incremental Term Loan. NEW definition.

'Third Amendment Incremental Revolving Commitment' has the meaning assigned in the Third Amendment (i.e., the amount by which a Third Amendment Incremental Revolving Lender increases its Revolving Commitment on the Third Amendment Effective Date). NEW definition.

'Revolving Commitment' means each Lender's commitment set forth on the Commitment Schedule (or in an Assignment and Assumption), as reduced or increased under Section 2.09 and Section 9.04; a Lender's Revolving Exposure may never exceed its Revolving Commitment. AS AMENDED: as of the Third Amendment Effective Date the aggregate amount of the Lenders' Revolving Commitments is $255,000,000 (increased from $200,000,000).
units.notes: This is the headline revolver capacity change made by the Third Amendment.

units.description: 'Source Atlantic Acquisition' means the acquisition of all issued and outstanding Equity Interests of Source Atlantic Limited (a New Brunswick corporation) under the Share Purchase Agreement dated July 9, 2024 between Skyline Holdings Incorporated (vendor) and Lawson Products Canada (purchaser). NEW definition.
units.notes: Feeds both the Permitted Acquisition definition and the free-of-charge Total Net Leverage Ratio Adjustment in Section 6.12(b).

units.description: 'Permitted Acquisition' means (w) the TEquipment Acquisition, (x) the HISCO Acquisition, (y) the Source Atlantic Acquisition and (z) any other Acquisition by a Loan Party (or a Restricted Subsidiary that becomes a Loan Party concurrently) that satisfies clauses (a)-(k): (a) not hostile/contested; (b) same or related line of business; (c) no Default before or after on a pro forma basis; (d) 20 days' prior notice with draft documents, due diligence package and quality of earnings report for acquisitions with total consideration >= $50,000,000; (e) structured as an asset purchase, merger with a Loan Party surviving, or purchase of substantially all voting Equity Interests; (f) Borrower/Loan Party must be surviving entity in a merger; (g) target must have positive pro forma adjusted EBITDA; (h) pro forma compliance with Section 6.12 (including any Total Net Leverage Ratio Adjustment), Total Net Leverage Ratio at least 0.25x below the then applicable Section 6.12(b) level, and Availability plus Unrestricted Cash of at least $10,000,000; (i) all Section 5.13 collateral/guaranty actions taken; (j) 5 Business Days' prior officer's certificate with clause (h) calculations for acquisitions with consideration > $50,000,000; and (k) aggregate purchase consideration (including earnouts) for acquisitions of Persons that do not become Loan Parties and assets that do not become Collateral may not exceed $50,000,000 during the term of the Agreement. AS AMENDED: the Source Atlantic Acquisition is added as a named permitted acquisition (clause (y)) and clauses re-lettered.
units.notes: Clause (k) is a term-of-the-agreement shared cap for non-Loan-Party/non-Collateral acquisitions; clause (h) embeds a 0.25x cushion below the Section 6.12(b) level.

units.description: 'Applicable Percentage' is computed separately for (a) Revolving Lenders (share of aggregate Revolving Commitments, or of Aggregate Revolving Exposure once commitments terminate), (b) Initial Term Lenders, (c) Delayed Draw Term Lenders (with a separate funding-stage measure based on unused commitments), (d) First Amendment Incremental Term Lenders and, AS AMENDED, (e) Third Amendment Incremental Term Lenders (share of outstanding Third Amendment Incremental Term Loans). In each case a Defaulting Lender's commitments/loans are disregarded per Section 2.20.

'Class' distinguishes Loans/Borrowings (Revolving, Initial Term, Delayed Draw Term, First Amendment Incremental Term, Third Amendment Incremental Term or Swingline), Commitments (Revolving, Initial Term Loan, Delayed Draw Term Loan, First Amendment Incremental Term Loan, Third Amendment Incremental Term Loan or any other class under Section 2.09) and Lenders. AS AMENDED to add the Third Amendment Incremental Term Loan Class.

'Maturity Date' means the Revolving Credit Maturity Date, the Initial Term Loan Maturity Date, the Delayed Draw Term Loan Maturity Date, the First Amendment Incremental Term Loan Maturity Date, the Third Amendment Incremental Term Loan Maturity Date, or the maturity date of any new Class established under Section 2.09, as applicable. AS AMENDED to include the Third Amendment tranche.

'Term Lender', 'Term Loan' and 'Term Loan Commitment' are each AS AMENDED to include, respectively, Third Amendment Incremental Term Lenders, Third Amendment Incremental Term Loans and Third Amendment Incremental Term Loan Commitments alongside the Initial, Delayed Draw and First Amendment Incremental tranches.

'Arranger' AS AMENDED comprises three groups: (i) JPMorgan, BofA Securities and CIBC Bank USA for the Initial Term Loan Commitments, initial Revolving Commitments and Delayed Draw Term Loan Commitments; (ii) JPMorgan, TD Bank, BofA Securities, Regions Bank Capital Markets and Capital One for the First Amendment Incremental Term Loan facility; and (iii) NEW - JPMorgan, Wells Fargo, U.S. Bank, BofA Securities and TD Bank for the Third Amendment Incremental Term Loan Commitments, Third Amendment Incremental Term Loans and Third Amendment Incremental Revolving Commitments.

'Applicable Rate' is a five-category leverage-based pricing grid keyed to the Total Net Leverage Ratio: Category 1 (>3.75x): ABR/Canadian Prime 1.75%, Term Benchmark/RFR 2.75%, commitment fee 0.35%, ticking fee 0.35%; Category 2 (<=3.75x but >3.00x): 1.50%/2.50%/0.30%/0.30%; Category 3 (<=3.00x but >2.25x): 1.00%/2.00%/0.25%/0.25%; Category 4 (<=2.25x but >1.50x): 0.50%/1.50%/0.20%/0.20%; Category 5 (<=1.50x): 0.00%/1.00%/0.15%/0.15%. Category 2 applies until the first Compliance Certificate after the Effective Date. Rate changes take effect on delivery of financials/Compliance Certificate; failure to deliver puts pricing in Category 1 at the option of the Administrative Agent or request of Required Lenders. Retroactive true-up is required if financials or ratio calculations were incorrect.

'EBITDA' means Net Income plus add-backs (a)(i)-(xx) (Interest Expense; income tax expense net of refunds; depreciation and amortization; net losses on non-ordinary-course asset Dispositions permitted by Section 6.05; non-cash losses/expenses subject to a future cash-payment claw-back; Closing Date Transaction Expenses paid within 180 days of the Transactions; non-recurring/unusual expenses; 'run-rate' Cost Savings projected in good faith and realizable within 24 months, subject to officer certification; purchase price adjustment/earnout/deferred comp fees; transaction fees for permitted Dispositions, equity/debt issuances and Permitted Acquisitions (whether or not consummated) and insurance-reimbursed casualty costs; director fees and expenses; officer board-meeting expenses capped at $250,000 per four-quarter period; insured business interruption expenses; amendment fees and expenses on the Loan Documents disclosed to the Administrative Agent; indemnified or third-party reimbursable fees; non-recurring/unusual/extraordinary non-cash charges; other non-cash charges; Acquired EBITDA of acquisitions for the trailing 12 months plus acquisition-related cost savings realizable within 24 months; integration/transition expenses; and non-cash equity-compensation expense), minus (b)(i)-(vi) (cash payments for prior-period non-cash charges; extraordinary/non-recurring gains and non-cash income; gains on non-ordinary-course dispositions; Disposed EBITDA for the trailing 12 months; gains on Section 6.05 Dispositions; and non-cash gains/income). All add-backs under (a)(vii), (a)(viii) and (a)(xviii)(b) are jointly capped at 20% of EBITDA calculated before such add-backs (the 'Combined Cap'). EBITDA for the four quarters of 2021 is fixed at $24,044,000 (Q1), $26,146,000 (Q2), $23,253,000 (Q3) and $21,919,000 (Q4).
units.notes: The 20% Combined Cap is a shared cap across three add-back categories - a classic basket-sharing relationship.

units.description: 'Applicable EBITDA' means EBITDA of the Company and its Restricted Subsidiaries for the four consecutive fiscal quarters most recently ended for which financials have been delivered under Section 5.01(a) or (b) (or, before the first such delivery, the Section 3.04(a) financials). It is the measure that grows the percentage-based baskets in Sections 6.01, 6.02, 6.04 and 6.05.

'Total Indebtedness' means the aggregate principal amount of all Indebtedness of the Company and its Restricted Subsidiaries on a consolidated basis, excluding clauses (i) (letters of credit/letters of guaranty reimbursement obligations) and (m) (Swap Agreement obligations) of the 'Indebtedness' definition.

'Total Net Leverage Ratio' means, on any date, Total Indebtedness minus Unrestricted Cash (netting capped at $50,000,000) divided by EBITDA for the four most recently ended consecutive fiscal quarters. Operating leases reflected on the consolidated balance sheet are excluded from the calculation.
'Total Net Leverage Ratio Adjustment' has the meaning in Section 6.12(b) - the temporary step-up of the maximum permitted Total Net Leverage Ratio following a Material Acquisition.

'Interest Coverage Ratio' means, for any four consecutive fiscal quarters, EBITDA divided by Consolidated Interest Expense, with an annualization convention for the four 2022 'Annualized Quarters' (multiplying post-Effective Date Consolidated Interest Expense by 4, 2, 4/3 or 1 for the quarters ending March 31, June 30, September 30 and December 31, 2022 respectively).

'Consolidated Interest Expense' means total interest expense (including on Capital Lease Obligations) of the Company and its Restricted Subsidiaries for the period on all outstanding Indebtedness, including LC and bankers' acceptance commissions, discounts and charges and net costs under interest rate Swap Agreements allocable to the period, on a consolidated GAAP basis. 'Interest Expense' is defined in substantially identical terms by reference to 'indebtedness'.

'Net Income' means consolidated net income (or loss) of the Company and its Restricted Subsidiaries under GAAP, excluding (a) income/deficit of any Person accrued before it became a Restricted Subsidiary or was merged into the Company or a Restricted Subsidiary, and (b) income/deficit of non-Restricted-Subsidiary Persons in which the Company or a Restricted Subsidiary holds an ownership interest, except to the extent actually received as dividends or similar distributions.

'Available Amount' is a builder basket equal to the sum of: (i) 25% of Applicable EBITDA (pro forma) as of the last day of the most recently ended four-quarter period; plus (ii) net cash proceeds of Qualified Stock issuances by the Company after the Effective Date that are not part of a Specified Equity Contribution and are Not Otherwise Applied; plus (iii) principal of Company Indebtedness issued after the Effective Date and exchanged/converted into Qualified Stock and Not Otherwise Applied; plus (iv) Returns received in cash or Permitted Investments from investments or Unrestricted Subsidiaries made using the Available Amount under Section 6.04(q), up to the original investment; plus (v) net cash proceeds from Dispositions of such investments or Unrestricted Subsidiary interests, up to the original investment; plus (vi) fair market value of investments in an Unrestricted Subsidiary redesignated as a Restricted Subsidiary (including via merger into, or transfer of substantially all assets to, a Borrower or Restricted Subsidiary), up to the original investment; plus (vii) Borrower Retained Prepayment Amounts; minus (viii) investments made under Section 6.04(q) and Restricted Payments made under Section 6.08(a)(iv) in reliance on the Available Amount since the Effective Date.
units.notes: Shared builder basket: Sections 6.04(q) and 6.08(a)(iv) both draw on, and both reduce, the same Available Amount.

units.description: 'Unrestricted Cash' means unrestricted cash and Permitted Investments held by the Loan Parties on a consolidated basis, but only to the extent subject to account control agreements in favor of the Administrative Agent; a 90-day post-First Amendment Effective Date grace applies to accounts of Subsidiaries acquired in the HISCO Acquisition.
units.notes: The control-agreement requirement is a gating condition for leverage netting and for the Permitted Acquisition liquidity test.

units.description: 'Indebtedness' is defined broadly in clauses (a)-(m): borrowed money; bonds/debentures/notes; obligations on which interest is customarily paid; conditional sale/title retention obligations; earn-outs and deferred purchase price (excluding ordinary-course trade payables, unaccrued earn-outs not on the balance sheet, accrued expenses and current accounts payable); Indebtedness of others secured by a Lien on the Person's property (capped at the lesser of the debt and the property's fair market value if not assumed); Guarantees; Capital Lease Obligations; letter of credit and letter of guaranty reimbursement obligations; bankers' acceptances; Off-Balance Sheet Liabilities; Disqualified Stock; and Swap Agreement obligations (including cancellations/terminations/assignments). Includes Indebtedness of entities for which the Person is liable by virtue of its ownership interest unless the terms provide otherwise.

'Permitted Encumbrances' comprises clauses (a)-(j): tax Liens not yet due or contested under Section 5.04; carriers'/warehousemen's/mechanics'/materialmen's/repairmen's and similar statutory Liens not overdue by more than 60 days or contested; workers' compensation/unemployment/social security pledges; bid, trade contract, lease, statutory, surety, appeal and performance bond deposits; judgment Liens not constituting an Event of Default under Section 7.01(k); easements, zoning restrictions and rights-of-way not securing monetary obligations; commodity/brokerage account margin and initial deposits; contractual setoff rights (depository relations, pooled deposit/sweep accounts, purchase orders); security given to public utilities or Governmental Authorities; and Governmental Authority Liens for Canadian Priority Payables not yet due or contested. Permitted Encumbrances exclude any Lien securing Indebtedness except under clauses (d) and (e).

'Permitted Investments' means (a) direct or guaranteed U.S. or Canadian federal government obligations maturing within one year; (b) commercial paper maturing within 270 days with the highest S&P or Moody's rating; (c) CDs, bankers' acceptances and time deposits maturing within 180 days with U.S./Canadian commercial banks having combined capital, surplus and undivided profits of at least $500,000,000; (d) fully collateralized repurchase agreements of not more than 30 days with such institutions; and (e) money market funds complying with SEC Rule 2a-7, rated AAA by S&P and Aaa by Moody's, with portfolio assets of at least $5,000,000,000.

'Permitted Supply Chain Financing' means one or more non-recourse supply chain financings, on terms reasonably satisfactory to the Administrative Agent, in respect of Supply Chain Financing Accounts owing by Account Debtors at the time such accounts were sold, provided each sale is a true sale with recourse limited to breach of a representation, warranty or covenant regarding the sold accounts. AS AMENDED the definition is keyed to the newly defined 'Supply Chain Financing Accounts'.
units.notes: Feeds Sections 6.01(o), 6.02(o) and 6.05(j) - a shared permission across the debt, lien and asset-sale covenants.

units.description: 'Supply Chain Financing Accounts' means any right to payment of a monetary obligation, whether or not earned by performance, arising in connection with goods sold or services rendered (including service charges, finance charges, interest and fees), together with the related Supply Chain Financing Related Assets. 'Supply Chain Financing Related Assets' means, for each such account, related contract rights and remedies (bills of lading, bills of exchange, promissory notes, accessions), supporting guaranties/suretyships/letters of credit/security/Liens, related books and records (including electronic), related insurance and all proceeds. NEW definitions.

'Material Acquisition' means (a) the TEquipment Acquisition, (b) the HISCO Acquisition and (c) any acquisition consummated after the First Amendment Effective Date with aggregate total consideration in excess of $75,000,000. This definition gates eligibility for the Total Net Leverage Ratio Adjustment under Section 6.12(b).

'Material Indebtedness' means Indebtedness (other than the Loans and Letters of Credit) or Swap Agreement obligations of the Company and its Restricted Subsidiaries exceeding $20,000,000 in aggregate principal amount; for Swap Agreements the principal amount is the net termination amount. Drives the cross-default Events of Default in Sections 7.01(f) and (g).

'Material Subsidiary' means each Restricted Subsidiary (other than non-U.S. and non-Canadian Subsidiaries) contributing more than 5% of EBITDA for the most recent four-quarter period or more than 5% of Consolidated Total Assets; if non-Material Subsidiaries in the aggregate exceed 10% of EBITDA or 10% of Consolidated Total Assets, the Company (or the Administrative Agent after 10 days) must designate additional U.S. Subsidiaries first and then Canadian Subsidiaries as Material Subsidiaries to eliminate the excess.
units.notes: Determines which Subsidiaries must join as Loan Guarantors under Section 5.13 - an entity-applicability driver.

units.description: 'Change in Control' means (a) any Person or group other than a Permitted Owner acquiring beneficial or record ownership of Equity Interests representing more than 30% of the aggregate ordinary voting power of the Company; (b) a majority of the Company's board seats being occupied by persons who were not directors on the date of the Agreement, nominated or appointed by the board, or appointed by such directors; or (c) the Company ceasing to own, free and clear of Liens other than Permitted Encumbrances and Liens securing Secured Obligations, at least 100% of the outstanding voting Equity Interests of the other Borrowers on a fully diluted basis. 'Permitted Owner' means any Person owning (directly or through Affiliates) more than 30% of such voting power as of the Effective Date.

'Restricted Subsidiary' means any Subsidiary other than an Unrestricted Subsidiary. 'Unrestricted Subsidiary' means any Subsidiary designated as such on Schedule 3.14 as of the Effective Date or designated by the Company's board under Section 5.15, in each case not subsequently redesignated as a Restricted Subsidiary. 'Subsidiary' means any direct or indirect subsidiary of a Borrower or other Loan Party; unstated references mean subsidiaries of the Company.

'Restricted Payment' means any dividend or other distribution (cash, securities or other property) on any Equity Interest in any Borrower or Restricted Subsidiary, or any payment (including sinking fund or similar deposits) on account of the purchase, redemption, retirement, acquisition, cancellation or termination of any such Equity Interests or any option, warrant or right to acquire them.

'Disposition'/'Dispose' means any sale, transfer, license, lease or other disposition of property (including a Sale and Leaseback Transaction and dispositions effected by Division), including sales or assignments of notes or accounts receivable with or without recourse.

'Prepayment Event' means (a)(i) any Disposition made in reliance on Section 6.05(k), (ii) any Disposition of all or substantially all assets of, or Equity Interests in, an Unrestricted Subsidiary, or (iii) any casualty, eminent domain taking or condemnation of property; or (b) the incurrence of any Indebtedness other than Indebtedness permitted under Section 6.01.
units.notes: Determines the scope of mandatory prepayments under Section 2.11(c); note that clause (a)(i) is limited to the general Section 6.05(k) disposition basket.

units.description: 'Net Proceeds' means, for a Prepayment Event, cash proceeds received (including cash received on non-cash proceeds when received, insurance proceeds in a casualty, and condemnation awards) minus (i) reasonable third-party fees and out-of-pocket expenses, (ii) payments required to repay Indebtedness (other than Loans) secured by the disposed asset or otherwise subject to mandatory prepayment, and (iii) taxes paid or reasonably estimated payable and reserves for directly attributable contingent liabilities in the year of the event or the following year.

'Required Lenders' means, before Loans become due and payable under Section 7.02 or Commitments terminate, Lenders holding more than 50% of the sum of Aggregate Credit Exposure and aggregate Unfunded Commitments (with Unfunded Commitments deemed zero solely for acceleration votes); afterwards, Lenders holding more than 50% of Aggregate Credit Exposure. Swingline Exposure in excess of a Lender's Applicable Percentage is excluded, and Affiliate Lenders are disregarded except as expressly permitted by Section 9.04(f).

'Affiliate Lenders' means LKCM Headwater Investments III, L.P. and its Affiliates (excluding the Company, its Subsidiaries and natural persons); 'Debt Fund Affiliate' means an Affiliate of LKCM Headwater Investments III, L.P. that is a Bona Fide Debt Fund with information barriers; 'Bona Fide Debt Fund' means a bona fide debt fund/investment vehicle/regulated banking or non-regulated lending entity primarily engaged in commercial loan or bond investing whose managers owe fiduciary duties to third-party investors independent of duties to the Company or LKCM (excluding natural persons and any Borrower or Subsidiary); 'Affiliate Lender Cap' has the meaning in Section 9.04(f).

'Disqualified Institutions' means Persons designated in writing by the Borrower Representative on or prior to the Effective Date as disqualified institutions or Competitors, plus Persons clearly identifiable by name as their Affiliates, subject to removal by written notice and to supplements effective two Business Days after delivery under Section 9.01 (non-retroactive as to existing holders). A Bona Fide Debt Fund is not a Disqualified Institution unless identified under clause (a)(i).

'Secured Obligations' means all Obligations together with all Banking Services Obligations and Swap Agreement Obligations owing to Lenders or their Affiliates, excluding any Excluded Swap Obligations of a Loan Guarantor. 'U.S. Secured Obligations' means all Obligations of the U.S. Loan Parties plus Banking Services Obligations and Swap Agreement Obligations of the U.S. Loan Parties and U.S. Subsidiaries. 'Canadian Secured Obligations' means all Obligations of the Canadian Loan Parties plus Banking Services Obligations and Swap Agreement Obligations of the Canadian Loan Parties and Foreign Subsidiaries; Canadian Secured Obligations expressly exclude U.S. Secured Obligations.
units.notes: The U.S./Canadian split is the backbone of the no-upstream-Canadian-guarantee/collateral structure - an entity-applicability driver throughout Articles V, VI, X and XI.

units.description: 'Loan Parties' means, collectively, the Canadian Loan Parties and the U.S. Loan Parties. 'U.S. Loan Party' means the U.S. Borrowers and the U.S. Loan Guarantors; 'Canadian Loan Party' means the Canadian Borrowers and the Canadian Loan Guarantors. Borrowers as of this Amendment are Distribution Solutions Group, Inc. (formerly Lawson Products, Inc.), Lawson Products, Inc. (Illinois), Baron Divestiture Company, Lawson Products Canada Inc., The Bolt Supply House Ltd., GS Operating, LLC and TestEquity LLC; Lawson Products Canada and Bolt Supply are the Canadian Borrowers.

Existing maturity dates as restated: 'Revolving Credit Maturity Date' = April 1, 2027 (or earlier termination/reduction to zero); 'Initial Term Loan Maturity Date' = April 1, 2027; 'Delayed Draw Term Loan Maturity Date' = April 1, 2027; 'First Amendment Incremental Term Loan Maturity Date' = April 1, 2027 - each subject to the next-succeeding-Business-Day convention.

First Amendment Incremental Term Loan Maturity Date

units.description: Existing facility sizes as restated: aggregate Initial Term Loan Commitments on the Effective Date $250,000,000; aggregate Delayed Draw Term Loan Commitments on the Effective Date $50,000,000 (available until the earlier of October 1, 2022 and termination); aggregate First Amendment Incremental Term Loan Commitments on the First Amendment Effective Date $305,000,000.
keyDefinedTerms: First Amendment Incremental Term Loan Commitment
Delayed Draw Term Loan Availability Period

units.description: 'Issuing Bank Sublimit' as of the Effective Date is $25,000,000 for JPMorgan and, for any other Issuing Bank, the amount it designates in writing; each Issuing Bank may increase or reduce its sublimit on five days' notice. 'Swingline Commitment' is the amount opposite JPMorgan's name on the Commitment Schedule. 'Issuing Bank' means JPMorgan, CIBC Bank USA (solely for the Existing Letters of Credit it issued) and any other Revolving Lender designated by the Borrower Representative with consent.

Interest rate definitions as restated for the SOFR/CORRA framework: 'Adjusted Term SOFR Rate' = Term SOFR Rate + 0.10%; 'Adjusted Daily Simple SOFR' = Daily Simple SOFR + 0.10%; 'Adjusted Term CORRA Rate' = Term CORRA + 0.29547% (one month) or 0.32138% (three month); 'Adjusted Daily Simple CORRA' = Daily Simple CORRA + 0.29547%; each subject to the 'Floor' (initially zero). 'Alternate Base Rate' = greatest of Prime Rate, NYFRB Rate + 0.50% and one-month Adjusted Term SOFR + 1.00%, with a stated 1.00% per annum floor. 'Canadian Prime Rate' = higher of the PRIMCAN Index and one-month Adjusted Term CORRA Rate + 1.00%, floored at 0%. 'Term Benchmark' refers to Adjusted Term SOFR or Adjusted Term CORRA; 'RFR' refers to Adjusted Daily Simple SOFR (Dollars) and Daily Simple CORRA (Canadian Dollars, only after a Term CORRA benchmark transition).
units.notes: CDOR was replaced with CORRA-based rates; the Second Amendment Effective Date definition preserves legacy CDOR loan economics until the then-current Interest Period expires.

units.description: 'Benchmark', 'Benchmark Replacement' (waterfall: (1) Adjusted Daily Simple SOFR for Dollars / Adjusted Daily Simple CORRA for Canadian Dollars, then (2) an Administrative Agent/Borrower-selected alternate plus the Benchmark Replacement Adjustment; reverting to the Adjusted Term CORRA Rate on a Term CORRA Reelection Event and Term CORRA Notice; floored at the Floor), 'Benchmark Replacement Adjustment', 'Benchmark Replacement Conforming Changes', 'Benchmark Replacement Date' (including a third trigger 30 days after a Term CORRA Notice), 'Benchmark Transition Event', 'Benchmark Unavailability Period', 'Term CORRA Reelection Event' and 'Term CORRA Notice' are defined to operate the Section 2.14 benchmark replacement machinery.

'Second Amendment Effective Date' means the date the Second Amendment to Amended and Restated Credit Agreement (dated June 13, 2024, between the Company and the Administrative Agent) became effective, anticipated to be June 28, 2024 to the extent the Benchmark Replacement Date for the CDOR Rate occurred then.

'First Amendment' means the First Amendment to Amended and Restated Credit Agreement dated as of the First Amendment Effective Date; 'First Amendment Effective Date' means June 8, 2023; 'HISCO', 'HISCO Acquisition', 'HISCO Acquisition Agreement' (Stock Purchase Agreement dated March 30, 2023 with GreatBanc Trust Company as ESOP trustee), 'HISCO Business' and 'HISCO Transactions' (the 'First Amendment Transactions') are defined and carried forward.
'Specified Equity Contribution', 'Cure Right' and 'Cure Expiration Date' each have the meanings given in Section 7.03 (the equity cure provision).

'Declined Amounts' and 'Borrower Retained Prepayment Amounts' have the meanings in Section 2.11(g) - mandatory prepayment amounts declined by Term Lenders and retained by the Borrowers, which then build the Available Amount. 'Asset Sale Prepayment Trigger' has the meaning in Section 2.11(c)(i).

'Capital Lease Obligations' means obligations to pay rent under leases required to be classified as capital or finance lease obligations under GAAP, measured at the capitalized amount; Section 1.04 freezes the pre-ASC 842 treatment for leases that would not have been capital leases under GAAP as in effect on December 31, 2015.

'Disqualified Stock' means Equity Interests that mature, are mandatorily redeemable, are redeemable at the holder's option, or are convertible into Indebtedness or other Disqualified Stock, in each case prior to 91 days after the latest Maturity Date, subject to change-of-control/IPO/asset-sale carve-outs conditioned on prior Payment in Full and to a management-equity exception. 'Qualified Stock' means Equity Interests other than Disqualified Stock.

'Dutch Auction' sets out the four-step auction procedure (Notice, Reply, Acceptance and Additional Procedures) by which the Company or a Subsidiary may purchase Term Loans of a Class: minimum $5,000,000 Auction Amount with $1,000,000 increments, a stated Discount Range, Return Bids in $1,000,000 increments, determination of the Applicable Discount, ratable scaling of Qualifying Bids, treatment of Failed Auctions and consummation through Section 9.04.

'Paid in Full'/'Payment in Full' requires (i) indefeasible cash payment of all Loans and LC Disbursements plus accrued interest, (ii) termination/cancellation of all Letters of Credit or cash collateral/backstop equal to 103% of LC Exposure, (iii) payment of accrued fees, (iv) payment of reimbursable expenses and other Secured Obligations (excluding unasserted Unliquidated Obligations), (v) termination of all Commitments, and (vi) termination of Swap Agreement Obligations and Banking Services Obligations or other satisfactory arrangements.
'Borrower Communications' and 'Borrower Portal' have the meanings assigned in Section 8.12 (the newly added borrower electronic-delivery platform provision).

'Material Adverse Effect' means a material adverse effect on (a) the business, assets, operations or financial condition of the Borrowers and Restricted Subsidiaries taken as a whole, (b) the ability of any Loan Party to perform its material Obligations, (c) the Collateral or the Administrative Agent's Liens on a material portion of the Collateral or their priority, or (d) the rights or benefits of the Administrative Agent, Issuing Bank or Lenders under the Loan Documents.

'Guarantee' means any contingent or other obligation guaranteeing, or having the economic effect of guaranteeing, Indebtedness or other obligations of another Person, including purchase-or-pay, keep-well, working-capital-maintenance and letter of credit support arrangements, but excluding endorsements for collection or deposit in the ordinary course; the amount is the stated or determinable amount of the primary obligation or, if not determinable, the maximum reasonably anticipated liability.

'Sanctions', 'Sanctioned Country' (listing the so-called Donetsk and Luhansk People's Republics, Crimea, Cuba, Iran, North Korea and Syria), 'Sanctioned Person', 'Anti-Corruption Laws', 'Canadian Economic Sanctions and Export Control Laws', 'OFAC', 'USA PATRIOT Act', 'CAML' and 'Beneficial Ownership Regulation/Certification' are defined for the compliance representations and covenants.

'Alternative Currency' means Canadian dollars plus any additional currency agreed after the Effective Date by the Borrower Representative, the Revolving Lenders, the Issuing Bank and the Administrative Agent (must be lawful, readily available, freely transferable and convertible into dollars); 'Agreed Currency' means dollars or any Alternative Currency. Related mechanics are in 'Dollar Equivalent', 'Equivalent Amount', 'Exchange Rate' and 'Revaluation Date'.
units.notes: Section 9.02(b)(I) makes any change to 'Alternative Currency' require each Revolving Lender's consent.

units.description: 'CAM', 'CAM Exchange', 'CAM Exchange Date' (the first date of a Section 7.01(h)/(i) insolvency event as to any Borrower or acceleration under Section 7.02), 'CAM Percentage' and 'Designated Obligations' (principal of and interest on Revolving Loans plus all commitment fees) define the Article XII collateral allocation mechanism among Revolving Lenders.

'Defaulting Lender' means a Lender that (a) failed within two Business Days to fund Loans or participations or pay amounts due (absent a good-faith condition-precedent notice), (b) publicly or in writing indicated it will not comply with funding obligations, (c) failed within three Business Days of a good-faith request to certify in writing that it will comply with and is financially able to meet its funding obligations, or (d) became subject to a Bankruptcy Event or Bail-In Action.

Interpretive sections as restated: 1.02 (classification of Loans/Borrowings by Class and Type); 1.03 (terms generally, UCC/PPSA definitions, and an extensive Quebec civil-law equivalence table); 1.04 (accounting terms and GAAP, with a GAAP-change negotiation freeze, exclusion of fair-value and convertible-debt bifurcation elections, and the FAS 842 lease grandfather to GAAP as in effect December 31, 2015); 1.05 (interest rate benchmark notification and Administrative Agent disclaimers, extended to Term CORRA Reelection Events); 1.06 (pro forma adjustments for acquisitions and dispositions, including that pro forma financial-covenant compliance is tested against the Section 6.12 levels for the quarter of the transaction without giving effect to any Total Net Leverage Ratio Adjustment except when testing Permitted Acquisition conditions, and that proceeds of newly incurred Indebtedness are not counted as Unrestricted Cash); 1.07 (Secured Obligations designated senior/designated senior indebtedness relative to Subordinated Indebtedness); 1.08 (rounding of financial ratios); 1.09 (Delaware-style divisions treated as transfers and new-entity acquisitions); 1.10 (exchange rates and currency equivalents, determined on each Revaluation Date and disregarded for financial statements and covenant calculations); and 1.11 (amendment and restatement of the 2019 credit agreement without novation, with continuation of commitments/loans, reallocation among Lenders, and reaffirmation of liens).
units.notes: Section 1.06's carve-out - Total Net Leverage Ratio Adjustment is disregarded for pro forma tests EXCEPT for Permitted Acquisition conditions - is easy to miss and can flip a capacity conclusion.

units.description: Commitments as restated: (a) Revolving Lenders severally make Revolving Loans in dollars, Canadian dollars or another Alternative Currency during the Availability Period, subject to each Lender's Revolving Commitment and the aggregate Revolving Commitments (revolving, so borrow/prepay/reborrow permitted); (b) Initial Term Lenders make Initial Term Loans in dollars on the Effective Date (no reborrowing); (c) Delayed Draw Term Lenders make Delayed Draw Term Loans during the Delayed Draw Term Loan Availability Period (no reborrowing); (d) First Amendment Incremental Term Lenders made First Amendment Incremental Term Loans on the First Amendment Effective Date (no reborrowing); and NEW clause (e) Third Amendment Incremental Term Lenders severally agree to make Third Amendment Incremental Term Loans in dollars to the Company on the Third Amendment Effective Date up to their Third Amendment Incremental Term Loan Commitments (no reborrowing). A closing flush provision confirms that no Canadian Loan Party is obligated to repay, support or guarantee any U.S. Secured Obligations and that payments by Canadian Loan Parties are applied only to Canadian Secured Obligations.
units.notes: Clause (e) is the new-money commitment created by this Amendment; the Canadian ring-fence flush language is an entity-applicability rule.

units.description: Borrowings must consist of Loans of the same Class, Type and Agreed Currency made ratably; Lender obligations are several. Dollar Revolving Borrowings are ABR or Term Benchmark; Canadian Dollar Revolving Borrowings are Canadian Prime Rate or Term Benchmark; Term Loan Borrowings are in dollars and are ABR or Term Benchmark; Swingline Loans are ABR dollar loans. Minimums: Term Benchmark Borrowings in multiples of $100,000 and at least $500,000; ABR/Canadian Prime Borrowings the same; Delayed Draw Term Loans in multiples of $1,000,000 and at least $5,000,000; Swingline Loans in multiples of $50,000 and at least $100,000. No more than twelve Term Benchmark and RFR Borrowings may be outstanding at any time. No Borrowing may have an Interest Period ending after the applicable Maturity Date.

Borrowing Requests are delivered by the Borrower Representative by hand, PDF email or approved Electronic System: three Business Days before a Term Benchmark Borrowing, by noon Chicago time on the date of an ABR or Canadian Prime Rate Borrowing (9:00 a.m. if financing an LC Disbursement reimbursement). Requests are irrevocable and must specify Class, Agreed Currency, aggregate amount and wire breakdown, Borrower(s), date, Type and (for Term Benchmark) Interest Period. Defaults apply if no election is made (ABR for dollars, Canadian Prime Rate for Canadian dollars, dollars if no currency, one-month Interest Period). Borrowers may not request RFR Loans in Dollars (Adjusted Daily Simple SOFR applies only under Sections 2.14(a) and (f)) or in Canadian Dollars prior to a Term CORRA benchmark transition.

Obligations denominated in dollars, Canadian dollars or an Alternative Currency are discharged only to the extent the payee can purchase the relevant currency with the payment currency on the next Business Day; each Borrower and Guarantor indemnifies for shortfalls (as a separate obligation notwithstanding any judgment) and excesses over the amount due plus Section 2.18(d) sharing are remitted back.

The Swingline Lender may (but is not obligated to) make dollar Swingline Loans to the U.S. Borrowers during the Availability Period subject to the Swingline Commitment, each Lender's Revolving Commitment and the aggregate Revolving Commitments; requests by noon Chicago time on the borrowing date and funded by 2:00 p.m. (b) The Swingline Lender may require Revolving Lenders to purchase absolute and unconditional participations in Swingline Loans in accordance with Applicable Percentages, unaffected by any Default or commitment termination. (c) and (d) provide for replacement of the Swingline Lender by written agreement and for resignation on 30 days' notice, with the replaced lender retaining rights on outstanding Swingline Loans.

Letters of Credit as restated: (a) issuance in Agreed Currencies during the Availability Period for obligations of Borrowers or Restricted Subsidiaries, with Sanctions, legal-restraint and Issuing Bank policy limitations; (b) three-Business-Day notice, a Letter of Credit Agreement is required, and issuance is conditioned on aggregate Dollar Equivalent LC Exposure not exceeding $25,000,000, no Revolving Lender exceeding its Revolving Commitment and Aggregate Revolving Exposure not exceeding aggregate Revolving Commitments, plus each Issuing Bank's individual Issuing Bank Sublimit (which the Issuing Bank may exceed in its discretion without affecting other sublimits or the aggregate LC cap); (c) one-year maximum tenor and expiry no later than five Business Days before the Revolving Credit Maturity Date unless cash collateralized at 103%; (d) automatic Revolving Lender participations at Applicable Percentages; (e) same/next Business Day reimbursement with the option to finance by ABR Revolving Borrowing, Swingline Loan or Canadian Prime Rate Borrowing; (f) absolute and unconditional reimbursement obligations with a care standard for the Issuing Bank; (g) disbursement procedures; (h) interim interest at the ABR or Canadian Prime rate; (i) replacement and resignation of an Issuing Bank; (j) cash collateralization at 103% of Dollar Equivalent LC Exposure in the LC Collateral Account upon an Event of Default (automatic for Section 7.01(h)/(i) events) or as required by Sections 2.11(b) or 2.20, with return within three Business Days after cure or waiver; (k) Issuing Bank reporting to the Administrative Agent; (l) LC Exposure determination conventions; (m) Letters of Credit issued for the account of Restricted Subsidiaries are the Borrowers' direct reimbursement obligations with waiver of suretyship defenses; and (n) Existing Letters of Credit are deemed issued under the Agreement.
units.notes: The $25,000,000 aggregate LC Exposure cap sits inside the (now $255,000,000) Revolving Commitments.

units.description: (a) Each Lender funds by wire by 2:00 p.m. Chicago time in an amount equal to its Applicable Percentage, with carve-outs for Initial Term Loans (Section 2.01(b)), First Amendment Incremental Term Loans (Section 2.01(d)), AS AMENDED Third Amendment Incremental Term Loans (Section 2.01(e)) and Swingline Loans (Section 2.05); proceeds are credited to the Funding Account, except LC reimbursement financings which are remitted to the Issuing Bank. (b) The Administrative Agent may assume Lender funding and, if not received, recover from the Lender at the greater of the Overnight Rate and interbank compensation rate, or from the Borrowers at the ABR Revolving Loan rate.

Borrowers may convert or continue Borrowings by irrevocable Interest Election Request delivered on the same timetable as a Borrowing Request; elections may not create a non-compliant Interest Period, convert to a Type unavailable for the Class, change currency, or elect Adjusted Daily Simple SOFR or Adjusted Daily Simple CORRA prior to the relevant benchmark transition. Failure to elect continues a Term Benchmark Borrowing for one month. During a continuing Event of Default and upon Required Lender request, no Term Benchmark conversions/continuations are permitted and Dollar Term Benchmark/RFR Borrowings convert to ABR and Canadian Dollar Term Benchmark/RFR Borrowings convert to Canadian Prime Rate. NEW clause (f) grandfathers legacy 'CDOR Loans' outstanding immediately prior to the Second Amendment Effective Date at the old CDOR Rate until the end of the then-current Interest Period, with the Applicable Rate for Term Benchmark Loans applying from the Second Amendment Effective Date.

Termination/reduction of Commitments and the incremental facility, as restated: (a) commitment termination events for the Initial Term Loan Commitments, the Revolving Commitments (Revolving Credit Maturity Date), the Delayed Draw Term Loan Commitments, the First Amendment Incremental Term Loan Commitments and NEW clause (v) the Third Amendment Incremental Term Loan Commitments (which terminate on the earlier of funding on, or 5:00 p.m. Chicago time on, the Third Amendment Effective Date); (b) voluntary termination on Payment in Full; (c) voluntary reductions in $1,000,000 multiples and not less than $1,000,000, subject to no Revolving Exposure overhang; (d) three Business Days' irrevocable (or conditional) notice, permanent and ratable reductions; (e) INCREMENTAL FACILITY - the Borrowers may increase Revolving Commitments or incur Incremental Term Loans (including increasing an existing tranche) from Lenders or other institutions (excluding Ineligible Institutions), provided (i) each request is at least $5,000,000, (ii) AS AMENDED the aggregate additional Revolving Commitments plus Incremental Term Loans incurred AFTER THE THIRD AMENDMENT EFFECTIVE DATE may not exceed $300,000,000, (iii) Administrative Agent (and, for revolving increases, Swingline Lender and Issuing Bank) approval of any new Lender, (iv) assumption of Lender rights and obligations, (v) satisfaction of Section 2.09(f), and (vi) Affiliate Lender compliance with Section 9.04(f); (f) conditions precedent - Loan Party officer's certificate with resolutions, bring-down of Article III representations, no Default, and pro forma compliance with Section 6.12 (including any applicable Total Net Leverage Ratio Adjustment) assuming the increase is fully drawn, plus opinions and documents; (g) settlement mechanics on revolving increases (deemed repayment and reborrowing with Section 2.16 break funding), plus the requirements that Incremental Term Loans rank pari passu with the Revolving Loans, Initial Term Loans, Delayed Draw Term Loans, First Amendment Incremental Term Loans AND (AS AMENDED) Third Amendment Incremental Term Loans, may not mature earlier than the latest Maturity Date, may not have a shorter weighted average life, must be treated no more favorably than the existing facilities, and are subject to a 50 basis point MFN: if the All-In Yield on Incremental Term Loans exceeds that of the Initial, Delayed Draw, First Amendment Incremental or (AS AMENDED) Third Amendment Incremental Term Loans by more than 50 basis points, the Applicable Rates on those existing tranches are increased so the differential is exactly 50 basis points; (h) implementation by an Incremental Facility Amendment executed by the Borrowers, the participating Lenders and the Administrative Agent, which may make necessary conforming amendments without other Lender consent and permits the Administrative Agent to revise the Commitment Schedule; (i) KYC/PATRIOT Act deliverables for new lending institutions.
units.notes: Two capacity changes interact: Section 2(a) of the Amendment temporarily lifted the old cap from $200,000,000 to $255,000,000 to permit this deal, and the restated Section 2.09(e)(ii) then resets the cap to $300,000,000 measured from the Third Amendment Effective Date - so the $200,000,000 term loan and $55,000,000 revolver increase funded under this Amendment do NOT consume the reset $300,000,000 basket. Also note the MFN now protects the new tranche.

units.description: Repayment and amortization as restated: (a) Revolving Loans due on the Revolving Credit Maturity Date and Swingline Loans on the earlier of that date and the fifth Business Day after funding (with automatic repayment from Revolving Loan proceeds); (b)(i) Initial Term Loans amortize $3,125,000 quarterly from June 30, 2022; (ii) Delayed Draw Term Loans amortize 1.25% of the original funded amount quarterly; (iii) First Amendment Incremental Term Loans amortize $3,812,500 quarterly from September 30, 2023; and NEW (iv) Third Amendment Incremental Term Loans amortize $2,500,000 quarterly on the last day of each March, June, September and December commencing December 31, 2024, with the balance due on the Third Amendment Incremental Term Loan Maturity Date; (c)-(g) Lender and Administrative Agent account records are prima facie evidence, Borrowers select which Term Loan Borrowings are repaid on three Business Days' notice with ratable application, and Lenders may request promissory notes.
keyDefinedTerms: Third Amendment Incremental Term Loan Maturity Date
units.notes: The new $2,500,000 quarterly amortization on a $200,000,000 tranche is 1.25% per quarter (5% per annum).

units.description: Prepayments as restated: (a) voluntary prepayment at any time without premium or penalty subject to notice and Section 2.16 break funding; (b) mandatory revolver paydown/cash collateralization whenever Dollar Equivalent Aggregate Revolving Exposure exceeds aggregate Revolving Commitments, with a 102% currency-fluctuation cushion and a two-consecutive-Business-Day limit; (c) mandatory Term Loan prepayment of 100% of Net Proceeds of any Prepayment Event within three Business Days (asset/casualty events) or one Business Day (non-permitted Indebtedness), subject to (i) a $10,000,000 per fiscal year Asset Sale Prepayment Trigger threshold (only amounts above the threshold are swept) and (ii) a reinvestment right of 12 months, extended by 180 days if a binding commitment is entered into within the 12-month period; (d) notice mechanics and ratable application; (e) application waterfall - ratably across all Classes of Term Loans and, within a Class, first to accrued interest and then ratably to the first four scheduled repayments and thereafter ratably to remaining scheduled repayments including the payment due at maturity; (f) foreign-subsidiary repatriation carve-outs for legally prohibited or materially adverse tax consequences, with the non-application not constituting a Default; and (g) each Term Lender may decline its share of a mandatory prepayment by Rejection Notice, with Declined Amounts retained by the Borrowers as Borrower Retained Prepayment Amounts.
units.notes: Declined Amounts feed the Available Amount builder basket, linking the prepayment waterfall to Sections 6.04(q) and 6.08(a)(iv) capacity.

units.description: (a) Commitment fee at the Applicable Rate on the undrawn Revolving Commitment (LC Exposure counted as drawn, Swingline Exposure excluded) and ticking fee at the Applicable Rate on unused Delayed Draw Term Loan Commitments, payable in arrears on the fifteenth day following each quarter end and at termination, computed on a 360-day year; (b) LC participation fees at the Term Benchmark Applicable Rate and Issuing Bank fronting fees and standard charges, payable on the same schedule; (c) agency fees as separately agreed; (d) all fees paid in dollars in immediately available funds and non-refundable.

Interest as restated: ABR Borrowings at the Alternate Base Rate plus the Applicable Rate; Canadian Prime Rate Borrowings at the Canadian Prime Rate plus the Applicable Rate; Term Benchmark Borrowings at the Adjusted Term SOFR Rate or Adjusted Term CORRA Rate plus the Applicable Rate; RFR Loans at Adjusted Daily Simple SOFR or Adjusted Daily Simple CORRA plus the Applicable Rate. (d) During a continuing Event of Default the Administrative Agent or Required Lenders may impose 2% default interest on Loans, a 2% increase to Section 2.12(b) fees and 2% on other overdue amounts. (e) Interest payable in arrears on Interest Payment Dates and on repayment/prepayment/conversion. (f) 360-day year except Prime Rate, Term CORRA, Daily Simple CORRA and Canadian Prime Rate computations (365/366). (g) Interest Act (Canada) disclosure. (h) Criminal Code (Canada) criminal-rate savings provision with a prescribed reduction order and reimbursement mechanism.

Benchmark machinery as restated for SOFR/CORRA: (a) inability to ascertain, or Required Lender notice that a rate will not adequately reflect cost, converts Dollar Term Benchmark requests to RFR (or ABR) Borrowings and Canadian Dollar Term Benchmark requests to Canadian Prime Rate Borrowings, with corresponding conversions of outstanding Loans; (b) automatic Benchmark Replacement on a Benchmark Transition Event and Benchmark Replacement Date (clause (1) replacements apply without consent; clause (2) replacements apply on the fifth Business Day after notice absent Required Lender objection); (c)(i) the Administrative Agent may implement Benchmark Replacement Conforming Changes without consent and (ii) NEW - upon a Term CORRA Reelection Event and delivery of a Term CORRA Notice, Canadian Dollar loans revert to the Adjusted Term CORRA Rate without further consent (delivery of the notice is discretionary); (d) notice obligations and conclusive determinations; (e) tenor removal and reinstatement; (f) Benchmark Unavailability Period consequences, including deemed conversions of requests and the exclusion of the affected benchmark component from ABR and Canadian Prime Rate.

Yield protection for reserve/liquidity requirements (excluding reserves reflected in the Adjusted Term CORRA Rate), other conditions or costs, and Taxes other than Indemnified Taxes, certain Excluded Taxes and Connection Income Taxes; plus capital and liquidity adequacy compensation. Certificates are conclusive absent manifest error, payable within ten days; claims are subject to a 180-day look-back limitation extended for retroactive Changes in Law.

Borrowers compensate Lenders for losses from off-cycle payments, conversions, failures to borrow/convert/continue/prepay, Section 2.19 or 9.02(d) assignments, and failures to pay Alternative Currency amounts on the scheduled due date; a parallel provision applies to term RFR Loans. Certificates are conclusive absent manifest error and payable within ten days.

Payments are made free of Taxes except as required by law, with gross-up for Indemnified Taxes; Loan Parties pay Other Taxes, provide evidence of payment, and jointly and severally indemnify each Recipient within ten days of demand. Lenders severally indemnify the Administrative Agent for Indemnified Taxes attributable to them, Participant Register failures and Excluded Taxes, with setoff rights. Detailed Lender status documentation requirements follow (IRS Forms W-9, W-8BEN/BEN-E, W-8ECI, W-8IMY, U.S. Tax Compliance Certificates in the forms of Exhibits C-1 through C-4, and FATCA documentation), with refund-sharing, survival and definitional provisions.

(a) Payment mechanics and currency rules; (b) the application waterfall for Collateral proceeds and, at the Administrative Agent's election or Required Lenders' direction after an Event of Default, for all payments: first Administrative Agent/Swingline Lender/Issuing Bank fees, indemnities and expenses; second Lender fees, indemnities and expenses; third accrued interest ratably; fourth principal, unreimbursed LC Disbursements and Swap Agreement Obligations and Banking Services Obligations (up to the most recent Section 2.22 notice amount) ratably; fifth 103% of aggregate LC Exposure as cash collateral; and sixth any other Secured Obligation - with amounts from a Loan Party never applied to that Loan Party's Excluded Swap Obligations and with Banking Services/Swap obligations excluded from the waterfall (and paid at the sixth tier) if no Section 2.22 notice has been given; (c) reserved; (d) pro rata sharing of setoffs through purchases of participations; (e) Administrative Agent may presume payment and claw back; (f) account statements are for convenience and estimates only.
units.notes: The Section 2.22 notice requirement is what determines whether hedge and cash-management claims share pari passu at the fourth tier or drop to the sixth tier.

units.description: (a) A Lender claiming Section 2.15 compensation or triggering Section 2.17 gross-up must use reasonable efforts to designate a different lending office if that would reduce the amounts and not be disadvantageous, at the Borrowers' cost; (b) the Borrowers may require such a Lender, or any Defaulting Lender, to assign its interests to an eligible assignee (not an Ineligible Institution; Affiliate Lender assignees must comply with Section 9.04(f)), subject to Administrative Agent (and where applicable Issuing Bank and Swingline Lender) consent, payment in full of the assigning Lender, and an actual reduction in the compensation or payments.

While a Lender is a Defaulting Lender: (a) commitment fees stop accruing on its Unfunded Commitments; (b) payments to it are applied through an eight-tier waterfall (Administrative Agent, Issuing Bank/Swingline Lender, LC cash collateralization, funding shortfalls, escrow for future funding and LC exposure, judgments in favor of Lenders/Issuing Banks/Swingline Lender, judgments in favor of Borrowers, then to the Defaulting Lender); (c) it loses voting rights and its exposure is excluded from Required Lender calculations except for amendments requiring its own or each directly affected Lender's consent; (d) its Swingline and LC Exposure is reallocated to non-Defaulting Lenders up to their Revolving Commitments, and otherwise prepaid or cash collateralized within one Business Day, with corresponding fee adjustments; (e) the Swingline Lender and Issuing Bank need not extend new credit unless 103% covered or cash collateralized. A Parent Bankruptcy Event or Bail-In Action, or a good-faith belief of default under other credit agreements, similarly excuses new Swingline Loans and Letters of Credit. Cure of Defaulting Lender status triggers readjustment and par purchases.

If the Administrative Agent or any Lender must surrender a payment (including by setoff) because it is invalidated, declared fraudulent, set aside, or determined to be a voidable preference, impermissible setoff or diversion of trust funds, the Obligations intended to be satisfied are revived and the Agreement continues in full force; the provision survives termination.

Each Lender or Affiliate providing Banking Services or Swap Agreements to a Loan Party or Restricted Subsidiary must promptly notify the Administrative Agent in writing of the aggregate amount of the related obligations and update on significant changes or request; the most recent information determines the Section 2.18(b) waterfall tier. JPMorgan and its Affiliates are exempt from this notice requirement while JPMorgan is Administrative Agent.
units.notes: The JPMorgan exemption means JPMorgan hedge/cash-management claims sit in the fourth waterfall tier without notice, unlike other providers.

articles.heading: Representations and Warranties (as amended and restated)

units.description: Organization; Powers - each Loan Party and Restricted Subsidiary is duly organized, validly existing and in good standing, has requisite power and authority, and is qualified in each jurisdiction where required except where failure could not reasonably be expected to result in a Material Adverse Effect. (Article III representations are brought down as a condition to the effectiveness of this Amendment under Section 4(b) and to each Credit Event under Section 4.02.)

Authorization; Enforceability - the Transactions are within each Loan Party's organizational powers and duly authorized; each Loan Document is duly executed and constitutes a legal, valid and binding obligation subject to bankruptcy and equitable principles. (Article III representations are brought down as a condition to the effectiveness of this Amendment under Section 4(b) and to each Credit Event under Section 4.02.)

Governmental Approvals; No Conflicts - the Transactions require no consents or filings except those obtained and perfection filings and those whose absence could not reasonably be expected to cause a Material Adverse Effect, do not violate any Requirement of Law, do not violate or cause a default under material agreements (subject to a Material Adverse Effect qualifier), and do not create Liens other than under the Loan Documents. (Article III representations are brought down as a condition to the effectiveness of this Amendment under Section 4(b) and to each Credit Event under Section 4.02.)

Financial Condition; No Material Adverse Change - the audited consolidated financial statements for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2021 (reported on by BDO USA LLP) present fairly in all material respects; no Material Adverse Effect has occurred since December 31, 2021. (Article III representations are brought down as a condition to the effectiveness of this Amendment under Section 4(b) and to each Credit Event under Section 4.02.)

Properties, etc. - Schedule 3.05 lists owned/leased real property as of the date of the Agreement; leases are valid and in full force; Loan Parties have good and indefeasible title or valid leasehold interests free of Liens other than those permitted by Section 6.02; registered IP is listed on Schedule 3.05 and its use does not materially infringe third-party rights. (Article III representations are brought down as a condition to the effectiveness of this Amendment under Section 4(b) and to each Credit Event under Section 4.02.)

Litigation and Environmental Matters - except for Disclosed Matters (Schedule 3.06), no litigation with a reasonable possibility of a materially adverse determination or involving the Loan Documents or Transactions; no material Environmental Liability notices or non-compliance except as could not reasonably be expected to cause a Material Adverse Effect; no adverse change in the status of Disclosed Matters. (Article III representations are brought down as a condition to the effectiveness of this Amendment under Section 4(b) and to each Credit Event under Section 4.02.)

Compliance with Laws and Agreements; No Default - compliance with all applicable Requirements of Law and binding agreements except where failure could not reasonably be expected to cause a Material Adverse Effect; no Default has occurred and is continuing. (Article III representations are brought down as a condition to the effectiveness of this Amendment under Section 4(b) and to each Credit Event under Section 4.02.)

Investment Company Status - no Loan Party or Subsidiary is an 'investment company' under the Investment Company Act of 1940. (Article III representations are brought down as a condition to the effectiveness of this Amendment under Section 4(b) and to each Credit Event under Section 4.02.)

Taxes - all required Tax returns filed and Taxes paid, except contested Taxes with adequate reserves or where failure could not be expected to cause a Material Adverse Effect; no material tax liens or claims. (Article III representations are brought down as a condition to the effectiveness of this Amendment under Section 4(b) and to each Credit Event under Section 4.02.)

ERISA - no ERISA Event has occurred or is reasonably expected that could reasonably be expected to result in a Material Adverse Effect, and Plan accumulated benefit obligations do not exceed Plan asset fair market value; as of the Effective Date no Canadian Pension Plan is a Canadian Defined Benefit Pension Plan, Schedule 3.10(b) lists all Canadian Pension Plans, and specified registration, administration, funding and contribution representations are given subject to a Material Adverse Effect qualifier. (Article III representations are brought down as a condition to the effectiveness of this Amendment under Section 4(b) and to each Credit Event under Section 4.02.)

Disclosure - all agreements, instruments and restrictions that could reasonably be expected to cause a Material Adverse Effect have been disclosed; written information furnished (taken as a whole) contains no material misstatement or omission, with the customary projections qualification; the Beneficial Ownership Certification is true and correct in all respects as of the Effective Date. (Article III representations are brought down as a condition to the effectiveness of this Amendment under Section 4(b) and to each Credit Event under Section 4.02.)

Solvency - immediately after the Effective Date Transactions and each Loan and Letter of Credit, the Loan Parties taken as a whole satisfy the balance-sheet, fair-saleable-value, ability-to-pay and adequate-capital solvency tests, and each Canadian Loan Party is not an Insolvent Person under the Bankruptcy and Insolvency Act (Canada); no Loan Party intends to incur debts beyond its ability to pay. (Article III representations are brought down as a condition to the effectiveness of this Amendment under Section 4(b) and to each Credit Event under Section 4.02.)

Insurance - Schedule 3.13 describes all insurance maintained as of the Effective Date; premiums due have been paid; the Loan Parties believe the insurance is adequate and customary. (Article III representations are brought down as a condition to the effectiveness of this Amendment under Section 4(b) and to each Credit Event under Section 4.02.)

Capitalization and Subsidiaries - as of the Effective Date Schedule 3.14 lists each Subsidiary and its relationship, each Borrower's authorized Equity Interests and record owners, entity types, and whether each Subsidiary is a Loan Party, Material Subsidiary, Restricted Subsidiary or Unrestricted Subsidiary; all issued Equity Interests owned by Loan Parties are duly authorized, fully paid and non-assessable. (Article III representations are brought down as a condition to the effectiveness of this Amendment under Section 4(b) and to each Credit Event under Section 4.02.)

Security Interest in Collateral - the Loan Documents create legal, valid, perfected and continuing Liens on all Collateral for the Secured Parties, having priority over all other Liens except Permitted Encumbrances entitled to priority by law or agreement and Liens perfected only by possession the Administrative Agent has not obtained, subject to making the specified UCC/PPSA/IP office filings and delivering certificated equity and notes. (Article III representations are brought down as a condition to the effectiveness of this Amendment under Section 4(b) and to each Credit Event under Section 4.02.)

Employment Matters - as of the Effective Date no strikes, lockouts or slowdowns; wage-and-hour compliance subject to a Material Adverse Effect qualifier; wages and benefit amounts paid or accrued. (Article III representations are brought down as a condition to the effectiveness of this Amendment under Section 4(b) and to each Credit Event under Section 4.02.)

Margin Regulations - no Loan Party is engaged principally in purchasing or carrying Margin Stock, no proceeds will be so used, and after applying proceeds not more than 25% of assets will be Margin Stock; no violation of Regulations U or X. (Article III representations are brought down as a condition to the effectiveness of this Amendment under Section 4(b) and to each Credit Event under Section 4.02.)

Use of Proceeds - Loan proceeds have been and will be used as set forth in Section 5.08. (Article III representations are brought down as a condition to the effectiveness of this Amendment under Section 4(b) and to each Credit Event under Section 4.02.)

No Burdensome Restrictions - no Loan Party is subject to Burdensome Restrictions except those permitted under Section 6.10. (Article III representations are brought down as a condition to the effectiveness of this Amendment under Section 4(b) and to each Credit Event under Section 4.02.)

Anti-Corruption Laws and Sanctions - policies and procedures are maintained to ensure compliance; Loan Parties, Subsidiaries and their officers, directors and (to knowledge) employees and agents are in material compliance and are not Sanctioned Persons; no Borrowing, Letter of Credit, use of proceeds or Transaction will violate Anti-Corruption Laws or Sanctions. (Article III representations are brought down as a condition to the effectiveness of this Amendment under Section 4(b) and to each Credit Event under Section 4.02.)

Affected Financial Institutions - no Loan Party is an Affected Financial Institution. (Article III representations are brought down as a condition to the effectiveness of this Amendment under Section 4(b) and to each Credit Event under Section 4.02.)

Plan Assets; Prohibited Transactions - no Loan Party or Subsidiary holds 'plan assets' under the Plan Asset Regulations and the transactions will not give rise to a non-exempt prohibited transaction under ERISA Section 406 or Code Section 4975. (Article III representations are brought down as a condition to the effectiveness of this Amendment under Section 4(b) and to each Credit Event under Section 4.02.)

Conditions to the original April 1, 2022 Effective Date, restated in full: (a) executed Credit Agreement, Loan Documents and U.S./Canadian legal opinions; (b) consummation of each Closing Date Acquisition in accordance with its agreement, absence of a Closing Date Material Adverse Effect since December 29, 2021, accuracy of Closing Date Acquisition Agreement Representations, no injunction, and delivery of specified audited, unaudited, projected, quality-of-earnings and pro forma financial information; (c) secretary's certificates, organizational documents and good standing certificates; (d) closing certificate as to no Default and accuracy of representations; (e) payment of fees and expenses and of accrued amounts under the prior credit agreement; (f) lien and IP searches; (g) payoff and release letters for Closing Date Target Indebtedness; (h) Funding Account notice; (i) solvency certificate; (j) pledged equity certificates, stock powers and pledged notes (with a five-day post-closing grace); (k) filings, registrations and recordings (with a thirty-day post-closing grace for items other than UCC/PPSA filings, certificated equity delivery and short-form IP filings); (l) insurance evidence; (m) letter of credit application; (n) completion of legal due diligence; (o) USA PATRIOT Act/KYC and Beneficial Ownership Certification deliverables; and (p) other requested documents. The Administrative Agent's notice of the Effective Date is conclusive, and the Commitments would have terminated if conditions were not satisfied by 2:00 p.m. Chicago time on June 30, 2022.
units.notes: Historical conditions; retained in the restated agreement but already satisfied. Not to be confused with the Amendment's own Section 4 conditions.

units.description: Each Loan (other than the First Amendment Incremental Term Loans, which were subject only to Section 4 of the First Amendment) and each issuance, amendment, renewal or extension of a Letter of Credit requires (a) representations true and correct in all material respects (in all respects for materiality-qualified representations; specified-date representations tested as of that date) and (b) no Default at the time of or immediately after the credit extension; each such credit event is a deemed representation to that effect. Notwithstanding failure of those conditions, the Administrative Agent and Issuing Banks may (but need not) continue to lend or issue for the ratable account and risk of the Lenders on the fifth Business Day after notice to the Lenders, absent written objection from Required Lenders.
units.notes: Note the restated carve-out is for First Amendment Incremental Term Loans only; the Third Amendment Incremental Term Loans were instead conditioned on Section 4 of the Third Amendment itself.

units.description: Reporting covenant: (a) audited annual consolidated financials within 90 days of fiscal year end (or earlier Form 10-K due date with automatic extensions), without going-concern or scope qualification; (b) quarterly consolidated financials within 45 days of each of the first three fiscal quarters (or earlier Form 10-Q due date); (c) a Compliance Certificate with each of (a) and (b), certifying fair presentation, whether a Default has occurred, detailed Section 6.12 calculations, and a Restricted/Unrestricted Subsidiary list where relevant; (d) annual Projections within 45 days after fiscal year end; (e) SEC and exchange filings and shareholder materials when publicly available; (f) SEC investigation correspondence; (g) audit reports and management letters on request; (h) other information on request, including KYC/Beneficial Ownership Regulation information; (i) Multiemployer Plan documents under ERISA Sections 101(k)(1) and 101(l)(1) on request; and (j) consolidating Restricted Subsidiary financials whenever Unrestricted Subsidiaries existed during the period. EDGAR or website posting satisfies delivery of (a), (b) and (e), subject to notice and paper-copy requests.
units.notes: Delivery of Section 5.01(a)/(b) financials is the trigger point for Applicable EBITDA, Applicable Rate changes and pro forma testing throughout the agreement.

units.description: Prompt written notice of: (a) any Default; (b) investigations or litigation seeking damages reasonably expected to exceed $5,000,000, injunctive relief over material assets, claims against a Plan, material criminal misconduct allegations, material Environmental Law violations or Environmental Liability, tax or governmental charge liability over $5,000,000, or a material product recall; (c) material changes in accounting or financial reporting practices (other than GAAP-required); (d) ERISA Events or Canadian Pension Events reasonably expected to result in aggregate liability exceeding $5,000,000; (e) any development resulting in or reasonably expected to result in a Material Adverse Effect; and (f) changes to the beneficial owners listed in the Beneficial Ownership Certification. Each notice must be accompanied by a Financial Officer statement of details and actions taken.
units.notes: Breach of Section 5.02(a) is an immediate Event of Default under Section 7.01(d) with no grace period; the balance of Section 5.02 gets a five-day cure under Section 7.01(e)(i).
