units.description: Each Loan Party and Restricted Subsidiary must preserve its legal existence and material rights, licenses, permits, franchises, governmental authorizations and intellectual property, and maintain requisite authority in each jurisdiction (subject to a Material Adverse Effect qualifier), and must conduct business in substantially the same manner and fields as presently conducted or reasonably related fields; mergers permitted by Section 6.03 are not prohibited.
units.notes: Failure as to a Loan Party's existence is an immediate Event of Default under Section 7.01(d).

units.description: Pay or discharge all Material Indebtedness and other material liabilities including Taxes before delinquency where non-payment could reasonably be expected to cause a Material Adverse Effect, except where contested in good faith with adequate GAAP reserves and non-payment pending contest could not reasonably be expected to cause a Material Adverse Effect.
Keep and maintain all property material to the conduct of business in good working order and condition, ordinary wear and tear excepted.

Keep proper books and records and permit Administrative Agent/Lender representatives (including consultants and appraisers) to visit and inspect properties, examine and extract from books and records and discuss affairs with officers and accountants, limited to one visit per year absent a continuing Event of Default; during a continuing Event of Default field examinations of assets, liabilities and books are permitted. Reports prepared by the Administrative Agent may be distributed to the Lenders.
units.notes: Breach carries the shorter five-day cure period under Section 7.01(e)(i).

units.description: Comply with each applicable Requirement of Law (including Environmental Laws) except where failure could not reasonably be expected to cause a Material Adverse Effect, and maintain and enforce policies and procedures designed to ensure compliance with Anti-Corruption Laws and applicable Sanctions.

AS AMENDED: (a) Initial Term Loan proceeds financed the Effective Date Transactions with the remainder for working capital and general corporate purposes; Revolving Loan, Swingline Loan and Letter of Credit proceeds are for working capital and general corporate purposes (including the Effective Date Transactions, Permitted Acquisitions and Restricted Payments); Delayed Draw Term Loan proceeds were solely for the TEquipment Acquisition and other Permitted Acquisitions and related fees; First Amendment Incremental Term Loan proceeds financed the HISCO Transactions with the remainder for working capital and general corporate purposes; and NEW - Third Amendment Incremental Term Loan proceeds will be used for working capital needs and general corporate purposes of the Borrowers and their Restricted Subsidiaries, including to finance, or to replenish cash previously used to finance, Permitted Acquisitions. No proceeds may be used in violation of Regulations T, U and X. (b) No Borrowing or Letter of Credit may be requested or used in furtherance of a payment violating Anti-Corruption Laws, to fund activities of or with a Sanctioned Person or in a Sanctioned Country (subject to a compliance carve-out), or in any manner violating applicable Sanctions.
units.notes: Breach of Section 5.08 is an immediate Event of Default under Section 7.01(d). The 'replenish cash previously used to finance Permitted Acquisitions' language expressly permits reimbursement of the Source Atlantic Acquisition funding.

units.description: All information furnished in connection with the Loan Documents or any amendment or waiver must contain no material misstatement or omission (taken as a whole, after supplements and updates), and furnishing information is a deemed representation to that effect; Projections need only be prepared in good faith on assumptions believed reasonable, with the customary forward-looking caveat.

Maintain with financially sound and reputable carriers insurance customary for similar businesses in similar locations of similar size (with no greater risk retention) and all insurance required by the Collateral Documents; furnish information at least annually on request.
Reserved.

Furnish prompt written notice of any casualty or insured damage to a material portion of the Collateral or commencement of eminent domain/condemnation proceedings, and ensure the Net Proceeds are collected and applied in accordance with the Agreement and the Collateral Documents.

(a) Within 30 days (or later as agreed) after a Person becomes a U.S. or Canadian Subsidiary that is also a Material Subsidiary, or after any U.S. or Canadian Subsidiary qualifies or is designated as a Material Subsidiary, the Company must notify the Administrative Agent and cause that Restricted Subsidiary to deliver a Joinder Agreement and a joinder to the applicable Security Agreement (with resolutions, organizational documents and, if requested, legal opinions), subject to a materially-adverse-tax-consequence and cost-benefit carve-out, whereupon it becomes a Loan Guarantor and grants Liens on its Collateral (excluding U.S. real property) - provided that no Canadian Loan Party may guarantee, support or provide Collateral for the U.S. Secured Obligations. (b) All owned property (other than Excluded Property) and 100% of the Equity Interests of directly owned Restricted Subsidiaries must remain subject to first-priority perfected Liens, subject to Section 6.02 Liens and the tax/cost carve-out; Canadian Loan Party Liens secure only the Canadian Secured Obligations. (c) Further assurances. (d) Newly acquired material assets must be notified and, if requested, subjected to Liens. (e) Three express limitations: no U.S. Secured Obligations are secured by Canadian Loan Party Collateral; no non-U.S./non-Canadian Collateral Documents or perfection actions are required; and the Administrative Agent may unilaterally waive perfection where cost is disproportionate to benefit.
units.notes: Core entity-applicability and collateral-scope provision; breach carries the five-day cure under Section 7.01(e)(i).

units.description: The Loan Parties must take the actions set forth on Schedule 5.14 by the dates specified there (or later dates agreed by the Administrative Agent in its sole discretion).
units.notes: Breach is an immediate Event of Default under Section 7.01(d); the underlying Schedule 5.14 is not restated in this Amendment (Schedules other than the Commitment Schedule remain as most recently delivered).

units.description: The Company may designate a Restricted Subsidiary as Unrestricted or an Unrestricted Subsidiary as Restricted provided that (a) before and after giving pro forma effect no Default exists and the Company is in pro forma compliance with Section 6.12; (b) no Loan Party may be designated Unrestricted; (c) no Subsidiary may be designated Unrestricted if it would then be a 'Restricted Subsidiary' for other secured Indebtedness; (d) no Unrestricted Subsidiary may own Equity Interests in a Restricted Subsidiary or hold a Lien on property of a Loan Party or non-designated Restricted Subsidiary; and (e) an Unrestricted Subsidiary may not own intellectual property material to the business (non-exclusive ordinary-course licenses permitted if the Company retains beneficial ownership and equivalent use rights). Designation as Unrestricted is an investment under Section 6.04 valued at the date of designation; redesignation as Restricted constitutes incurrence of that Subsidiary's investments, Indebtedness and Liens and a return on the investment.
units.notes: Designation consumes Section 6.04 investment capacity and can rebuild the Available Amount on redesignation - a shared-resource relationship.

units.description: Debt covenant lead-in: no Loan Party will, nor permit any Restricted Subsidiary to, create, incur, assume or suffer to exist any Indebtedness except as permitted by clauses (a) through (q).
Section 6.01(a) permits the Secured Obligations and the Guaranteed Obligations.

Section 6.01(b) permits indebtedness of any Borrower owing to any Restricted Subsidiary and of any Restricted Subsidiary owing to any Borrower or other Restricted Subsidiary, provided (i) Indebtedness of a non-Loan-Party Restricted Subsidiary owing to a Borrower or Loan Party is subject to Section 6.04, (ii) Indebtedness of a Loan Party owing to a non-Loan-Party Restricted Subsidiary must be subordinated to the Secured Obligations on terms reasonably satisfactory to the Administrative Agent, and (iii) the aggregate principal amount of Indebtedness of Restricted Subsidiaries that are not U.S. Loan Parties owing to U.S. Loan Parties, TOGETHER WITH outstanding Guarantees under Section 6.01(c)(iii) and outstanding investments by U.S. Loan Parties in non-U.S.-Loan-Party Restricted Subsidiaries under Section 6.04(b), may not exceed 15% of Applicable EBITDA.
units.notes: Clause (b)(iii) is a SHARED 15% of Applicable EBITDA cap across Sections 6.01(b)(iii), 6.01(c)(iii) and 6.04(b) - drawing on one reduces the others.

units.description: Section 6.01(c) permits guarantees by any Borrower of Restricted Subsidiary Indebtedness and by any Restricted Subsidiary of Borrower or other Restricted Subsidiary Indebtedness, provided (i) the guaranteed Indebtedness is itself permitted by Section 6.01, (ii) Guarantees by a Borrower or Loan Party of non-Loan-Party Restricted Subsidiary Indebtedness are subject to Section 6.04, and (iii) the aggregate principal amount of non-U.S.-Loan-Party Restricted Subsidiary Indebtedness Guaranteed by U.S. Loan Parties, together with Section 6.01(b)(iii) Indebtedness and Section 6.04(b) investments, may not exceed 15% of Applicable EBITDA.
units.notes: Same shared 15% of Applicable EBITDA cap as Sections 6.01(b)(iii) and 6.04(b).

units.description: Section 6.01(d) permits indebtedness owed to providers of workers' compensation, health, disability, other employee benefits or property/casualty/liability insurance under reimbursement or indemnification obligations incurred in the ordinary course.
Section 6.01(e) permits indebtedness of any Loan Party in respect of performance bonds, bid bonds, appeal bonds, surety bonds and similar obligations provided in the ordinary course of business.
Section 6.01(f) permits indebtedness existing on the date of the Agreement and listed on Schedule 6.01, and any Refinance Indebtedness in respect thereof.
units.notes: Schedule 6.01 is not restated by this Amendment and remains in the form most recently delivered.

units.description: Section 6.01(g) permits refinance Indebtedness extending, renewing, refinancing or replacing Schedule 6.01 Indebtedness, subject to six conditions: (i) no increase in principal (other than unused commitments, accrued interest, fees, defeasance costs, premiums, discounts and expenses of the refinancing), (ii) no extension of Liens to additional property (other than accessions/improvements/after-acquired property), (iii) no additional obligors, (iv) no shortening of weighted average maturity, (v) terms not less favorable to the obligor, and (vi) subordination terms at least as favorable to the Administrative Agent and Lenders where the original was subordinated.

Section 6.01(h) permits indebtedness of a Person designated as a Restricted Subsidiary after the date of the Agreement, provided it exists when the Person becomes a Restricted Subsidiary and was not created in contemplation thereof, and the aggregate principal amount under this clause may not exceed $20,000,000 at any time outstanding.

Section 6.01(i) permits customer deposits and advance payments (including progress payments) received in the ordinary course from customers for ordinary-course goods and services, to the extent constituting Indebtedness.

Section 6.01(j) permits indebtedness (i) in respect of Banking Services and other netting services, overdraft protection, employee credit card programs, automatic clearinghouse and similar deposit account arrangements incurred in the ordinary course and (ii) arising from a bank honoring a check or similar instrument drawn against insufficient funds in the ordinary course.

Section 6.01(k) permits obligations under letters of support, guarantees or similar obligations issued for the benefit of the Company or a Restricted Subsidiary to the extent required by law or in connection with statutory filings or audit opinions in non-U.S. jurisdictions, in the ordinary course.

Section 6.01(l) permits indebtedness consisting of (i) insurance premium financing or (ii) take-or-pay obligations in supply arrangements, incurred in the ordinary course or consistent with past practice.

Section 6.01(m) permits indebtedness (i) of the Company or a Restricted Subsidiary incurred, assumed or issued in connection with a Permitted Acquisition and (ii) of Persons acquired by, or merged/amalgamated/consolidated into, the Company or a Restricted Subsidiary pursuant to a Permitted Acquisition.
units.notes: Uncapped acquisition-debt basket - its size is limited only by the Permitted Acquisition conditions (including pro forma Section 6.12 compliance with a 0.25x cushion).

units.description: Section 6.01(n) permits indebtedness arising from customary indemnification, purchase price adjustment or similar obligations (including earn-outs) incurred or assumed in connection with a Permitted Acquisition (or other investment permitted by Section 6.04) or a Disposition permitted by Section 6.05.
Section 6.01(o) permits obligations under one or more Permitted Supply Chain Financings, to the extent constituting Indebtedness.
units.notes: Paired with the Lien permission in Section 6.02(o) and the Disposition permission in Section 6.05(j).

units.description: Section 6.01(p) permits indebtedness incurred to finance the acquisition, construction or improvement of fixed or capital assets (whether or not purchase money), including Capital Lease Obligations and assumed or pre-existing acquisition-asset debt, plus permitted refinancings under clause (g), provided (i) incurrence occurs prior to or within 180 days after the acquisition or completion and (ii) the aggregate principal amount under this clause, together with related Refinance Indebtedness, may not exceed 15% of Applicable EBITDA at any time outstanding.
units.notes: Paired with the Lien permission in Section 6.02(j), which cross-references this basket.

units.description: Section 6.01(q) permits other Indebtedness in an aggregate outstanding principal amount not exceeding at any time the greater of $25,000,000 and 25% of Applicable EBITDA.
units.notes: General debt basket; grows with Applicable EBITDA.

units.description: Lien covenant lead-in: no Loan Party will, nor permit any Restricted Subsidiary to, create, incur, assume or permit to exist any Lien on any property or asset now owned or hereafter acquired, or assign or sell any income or revenues (including Accounts) or rights in respect thereof, except as permitted by clauses (a) through (p).
Section 6.02(a) permits liens created pursuant to any Loan Document.
Section 6.02(b) permits permitted Encumbrances.
units.notes: Incorporates the ten-clause Permitted Encumbrances definition, which excludes Liens securing Indebtedness other than clauses (d) and (e) of that definition.

units.description: Section 6.02(c) permits liens on property of a Borrower or Restricted Subsidiary existing on the date of the Agreement and set forth on Schedule 6.02, provided the Lien does not extend to other property and secures only the obligations it secured on that date plus non-increasing extensions, renewals and replacements.

Section 6.02(d) permits liens existing on property before its acquisition by a Loan Party or Restricted Subsidiary, or on property of a Person before it becomes a Restricted Subsidiary (other than by redesignation of an Unrestricted Subsidiary), provided the Lien was not created in contemplation of the acquisition, does not extend to other property, and secures only the pre-existing obligations plus non-increasing extensions, renewals and replacements.

Section 6.02(e) permits collecting bank Liens under UCC Section 4-210 (or PPSA equivalent) covering only items being collected, and bankers' Liens and customary contractual setoff rights on funds and securities in accounts, not given in connection with the incurrence of Indebtedness.
Section 6.02(f) permits liens arising out of Sale and Leaseback Transactions permitted by Section 6.06.
Section 6.02(g) permits liens granted by a non-Loan-Party Restricted Subsidiary in favor of a Borrower or another Loan Party securing Indebtedness owed by that Restricted Subsidiary.

Section 6.02(h) permits liens (i) in favor of customs and revenue authorities arising by law to secure customs duties on ordinary-course imports and (ii) on specific inventory or goods and proceeds securing bankers' acceptances or documentary letters of credit issued to facilitate their purchase, shipment or storage in the ordinary course.

Section 6.02(i) permits liens arising out of conditional sale, title retention, consignment or similar arrangements for the sale of goods entered into in the ordinary course, provided the Lien does not extend to other property.

Section 6.02(j) permits liens on fixed or capital assets acquired, constructed or improved, provided (i) they secure Indebtedness permitted by Section 6.01(p), (ii) the Liens and secured Indebtedness are incurred prior to or within 180 days after the acquisition or completion, (iii) the secured Indebtedness does not exceed the cost of the assets and (iv) the Liens do not extend to other property.
units.notes: Directly tied to and capped by the Section 6.01(p) 15% of Applicable EBITDA basket.

units.description: Section 6.02(k) permits (i) Liens under workers' compensation, health, disability, unemployment insurance and similar employee-benefit legislation, good faith deposits for bids, tenders, non-debt contracts, leases and similar obligations, Liens securing public or statutory obligations, deposits of cash or U.S. government bonds securing surety, stay, customs, performance or appeal bonds, rent deposits and contractual/warranty refund deposits, in each case in the ordinary course; and (ii) Liens securing letters of credit, bankers' acceptances and bank guaranties supporting the foregoing.

Section 6.02(l) permits leases, franchises, grants, subleases, licenses, sublicenses, covenants not to sue, releases, consents and other forms of license (non-exclusive as to intellectual property) granted in the ordinary course that do not materially interfere with the business and do not secure Indebtedness.
Section 6.02(m) permits liens arising from UCC or similar financing statement filings regarding operating leases or consignments entered into in the ordinary course.
Section 6.02(n) permits purported Liens (other than Liens securing Indebtedness for borrowed money) incurred in the ordinary course and evidenced by precautionary UCC or similar public filings.
Section 6.02(o) permits liens (if any) on Accounts sold, or in the case of judicial recharacterization granted as collateral to secure financing, pursuant to any Permitted Supply Chain Financings.
Section 6.02(p) permits other Liens securing obligations in an aggregate principal amount at any time outstanding not exceeding the greater of $25,000,000 and 25% of Applicable EBITDA.
units.notes: General Lien basket; note it is sized identically to but is separate from the Section 6.01(q), 6.04(r) and 6.05(k) baskets.

units.description: Section 6.03(a) (Fundamental Changes): No Loan Party or Restricted Subsidiary may merge into or consolidate with any Person, permit another Person to merge or amalgamate into it, Dispose of all or substantially all of its assets or of all or substantially all stock of a Restricted Subsidiary, or liquidate or dissolve, except (with no Event of Default existing or resulting): (i) a Canadian Subsidiary of a Borrower may merge into a Borrower with a Borrower surviving (a U.S. Borrower must survive if a U.S. Borrower is involved); (ii) a U.S. Subsidiary of a Borrower may merge into a U.S. Borrower with the U.S. Borrower surviving; (iii) a Canadian Loan Party (other than a Borrower) may merge into another Loan Party with a Loan Party surviving (U.S. Loan Party must survive if involved); (iv) a U.S. Loan Party (other than a Borrower) may merge into another U.S. Loan Party with a U.S. Loan Party surviving; and (v) a non-Loan-Party Restricted Subsidiary may liquidate or dissolve if the Borrowers determine in good faith it is in their best interests and not materially disadvantageous to the Lenders; mergers involving a Person that is not a wholly owned Restricted Subsidiary must also be permitted by Section 6.04.
units.notes: Directional survivorship rules preserve the U.S./Canadian credit split.

units.description: Section 6.03(b) (Fundamental Changes): No Loan Party or Restricted Subsidiary may consummate a Division as the Dividing Person without the Administrative Agent's prior written consent; if a Loan Party that is an LLC nonetheless divides, each Division Successor that is a Material Subsidiary must comply with Section 5.13 and become a Loan Party.

Section 6.03(c) (Fundamental Changes): No Loan Party or Restricted Subsidiary may engage in any business other than businesses of the type conducted on the date of the Agreement and reasonably related businesses and reasonable extensions.
Section 6.03(d) (Fundamental Changes): No Loan Party or Restricted Subsidiary may change its fiscal year or any fiscal quarter from the basis in effect on the Effective Date.
Section 6.03(e) (Fundamental Changes): No Loan Party may change the accounting basis on which its financial statements are prepared except as required by GAAP or directed by the SEC.
Section 6.03(f) (Fundamental Changes): No Loan Party may change the tax filing elections it has made under the Code.

Section 6.03(g) (Fundamental Changes): No Loan Party or Restricted Subsidiary may contribute to, assume or cause an obligation to contribute to, or have any liability under, any Canadian Defined Benefit Pension Plan, or acquire an interest in any Person that sponsors, maintains or contributes to (or did so in the preceding five years) such a plan, without the Administrative Agent's prior written consent, not to be unreasonably withheld.
units.notes: An acquisition-blocking provision that operates independently of the Permitted Acquisition definition.

units.description: Investment covenant lead-in: no Loan Party will, nor permit any Restricted Subsidiary to, form any subsidiary after the Effective Date, or purchase, hold or acquire Equity Interests, evidences of indebtedness or other securities of, make or permit loans or advances to, Guarantee obligations of, or make or permit any investment or other interest in, any other Person, or acquire assets of another Person constituting a business unit, except as permitted by clauses (a) through (r).
Section 6.04(a) permits permitted Investments.

Section 6.04(b) permits investments by Loan Parties in Equity Interests of their Restricted Subsidiaries that are Loan Parties, provided such Equity Interests held by a Loan Party are pledged under the applicable Security Agreement, and provided further that the aggregate outstanding amount of investments by U.S. Loan Parties in Restricted Subsidiaries that are not U.S. Loan Parties made after the Effective Date, together with Section 6.01(b)(iii) Indebtedness and Section 6.01(c)(iii) Guarantees, may not exceed 15% of EBITDA.
units.notes: Third leg of the shared 15% cap with Sections 6.01(b)(iii) and 6.01(c)(iii). Note the text of this clause references '15% of EBITDA' whereas the two Section 6.01 legs reference '15% of Applicable EBITDA' - flagging the inconsistency rather than reconciling it.

units.description: Section 6.04(c) permits loans or advances by a Loan Party to another Loan Party or Restricted Subsidiary, and by a non-Loan-Party Restricted Subsidiary to a Loan Party or other Restricted Subsidiary, provided (i) loans and advances by a Loan Party are evidenced by a promissory note pledged under the applicable Security Agreement and (ii) loans and advances by U.S. Loan Parties to non-Loan-Party Restricted Subsidiaries are subject to Section 6.01(b)(iii), determined without regard to write-downs or write-offs.
units.notes: Also draws on the shared 15% cap.

units.description: Section 6.04(d) permits guarantees permitted under Section 6.01.
Section 6.04(e) permits notes payable, stock or other securities issued by account debtors pursuant to negotiated settlements of their Accounts in the ordinary course consistent with past practice.
Section 6.04(f) permits investments in the form of Swap Agreements permitted by Section 6.07.
Section 6.04(g) permits investments constituting deposits described in clauses (c) and (d) of the Permitted Encumbrances definition.
Section 6.04(h) permits permitted Acquisitions.
units.notes: Unlimited in amount but fully conditioned by the Permitted Acquisition definition, including its $50,000,000 term-of-agreement cap on acquisitions of non-Loan-Parties and non-Collateral assets.

units.description: Section 6.04(i) permits investments of any Person existing at the time it becomes a Restricted Subsidiary (other than by redesignation of an Unrestricted Subsidiary) or consolidates or merges with a Loan Party or its Restricted Subsidiaries (including in a Permitted Acquisition), so long as not made in contemplation of that event.
Section 6.04(j) permits the Closing Date Acquisitions.

Section 6.04(k) permits investments existing on the date of the Agreement and described on Schedule 6.04, and modifications, replacements, renewals, refinancings, reinvestments or extensions thereof, provided the amount is not increased except pursuant to the terms of the investment (including unused commitments), plus accrued interest (including PIK), premium, fees and expenses as in existence on the Effective Date.

Section 6.04(l) permits (i) Arms-length loans or advances (or Guarantees) by a Loan Party to its employees in the ordinary course consistent with past practice for travel, entertainment, relocation and similar purposes up to $5,000,000 outstanding at any time; and (ii) non-cash loans by a Loan Party or Restricted Subsidiary to officers, directors, governors, managers and employees used to simultaneously purchase Equity Interests (other than Disqualified Stock) of the Company.
Section 6.04(m) permits investments consisting of ordinary-course purchases and acquisitions of inventory, supplies, materials, equipment or similar assets, or of services.
Section 6.04(n) permits non-exclusive licensing of intellectual property (i) in the ordinary course or (ii) that does not materially interfere with the business and does not secure Indebtedness.

Section 6.04(o) permits deposits required by any Governmental Authority or public utility, including for Taxes and similar charges, to the extent the underlying obligations would not constitute an Event of Default.

Section 6.04(p) permits investments in prepaid expenses, negotiable instruments held for collection, and lease, utility, workers compensation, performance and similar deposits entered into in the ordinary course as a result of the operation of the business.

Section 6.04(q) permits other investments in an amount not exceeding the Available Amount immediately prior to the investment, so long as at the time and after giving pro forma effect (i) no Event of Default exists or would result and (ii) the Total Net Leverage Ratio is not greater than 0.5 to 1.00 lower than the maximum Total Net Leverage Ratio permitted under Section 6.12.
units.notes: Draws on the same Available Amount as Restricted Payments under Section 6.08(a)(iv) and carries a 0.5x leverage cushion condition.

units.description: Section 6.04(r) permits other investments, loans or advances in an aggregate outstanding amount not exceeding the greater of $25,000,000 and 25% of Applicable EBITDA determined when made, provided no Event of Default exists or would result.
units.notes: General investment basket.

units.description: Closing flush language for Section 5.15 and Section 6.04: 'investments' include the proportionate fair market value of a Subsidiary's net assets when designated an Unrestricted Subsidiary; on redesignation as a Restricted Subsidiary the Company is deemed to retain a permanent investment equal to the prior investment less the proportionate fair market value of net assets at redesignation (if positive); and property transferred to or from an Unrestricted Subsidiary is valued at fair market value at the time of transfer.

Asset sale covenant lead-in: no Loan Party will, nor permit any Restricted Subsidiary to, Dispose of any asset (including Equity Interests it owns), nor permit any Restricted Subsidiary to issue additional Equity Interests (other than to another Loan Party or Restricted Subsidiary in compliance with Section 6.04), except as permitted by clauses (a) through (k).

Section 6.05(a) permits dispositions of (i) inventory, goods or other assets in the ordinary course, (ii) obsolete, negligible, uneconomical, worn out or surplus property, (iii) assets no longer used or useful in the business, and (iv) other property (including leasehold interests) no longer economically practical.

Section 6.05(b) permits dispositions of assets to any Loan Party or Restricted Subsidiary, provided that Dispositions (i) involving a non-Loan-Party Restricted Subsidiary or (ii) from a U.S. Loan Party to a Canadian Loan Party or vice versa must comply with Section 6.09.
units.notes: Cross-border Loan Party transfers are routed through the affiliate transaction covenant.

units.description: Section 6.05(c) permits dispositions of Accounts (excluding factoring arrangements) in connection with their compromise, settlement or collection.

Section 6.05(d) permits dispositions of cash, Permitted Investments and other investments permitted by Sections 6.04(g) and (j); Dispositions constituting Liens permitted by Section 6.02; and Dispositions constituting Restricted Payments permitted by Section 6.08.

Section 6.05(e) permits (i) Sale and Leaseback Transactions permitted by Section 6.06 and (ii) Dispositions (including Sale and Leaseback Transactions) of real property or other fixed or capital assets acquired pursuant to the HISCO Acquisition, made for fair value and with aggregate fair market value not exceeding $20,000,000.
units.notes: Clause (e)(ii) is a dedicated $20,000,000 HISCO asset carve-out that is also excluded from the Section 6.06 180-day timing requirement.

units.description: Section 6.05(f) permits dispositions resulting from casualty, eminent domain taking, condemnation or similar proceedings affecting property of a Borrower or Restricted Subsidiary.
Section 6.05(g) permits foreclosures, condemnation, expropriation or similar actions, Dispositions required by a Governmental Authority, and casualty or insured damage to assets.

Section 6.05(h) permits disposition or discount of inventory, accounts receivable or notes receivable in the ordinary course, and conversion of accounts receivable to notes receivable in the ordinary course consistent with past practice.

Section 6.05(i) permits other than in respect of intellectual property, leases, assignments, subleases, licenses, sublicenses, covenants not to sue, releases, consents and other forms of license (and terminations) in the ordinary course that do not materially interfere with the business taken as a whole.
Section 6.05(j) permits dispositions resulting from sales of Accounts under Permitted Supply Chain Financings.

Section 6.05(k) permits dispositions of assets, including Sale and Leaseback Transactions not otherwise permitted by clause (e)(ii), not permitted by any other clause (excluding Equity Interests in a Borrower, and excluding Equity Interests in a Restricted Subsidiary unless all of them are sold), provided the aggregate fair market value of assets Disposed of in reliance on this clause may not exceed, during any fiscal year of the Company, the greater of $25,000,000 and 25% of Applicable EBITDA, and provided further that (other than as set forth on Schedule 6.05) all such Dispositions must be made for fair value and for at least 75% cash consideration.
units.notes: This is the only Disposition basket whose Net Proceeds trigger the Section 2.11(c) mandatory prepayment sweep via clause (a)(i) of the Prepayment Event definition. Note the annual (not cumulative) reset.

units.description: Overriding prohibition: notwithstanding the Section 6.05 exceptions, no Loan Party or Restricted Subsidiary may consummate any transaction resulting in the Disposition (by Restricted Payment, investment, Lien, sale, conveyance, transfer or otherwise, in a single transaction or series) of intellectual property material to the business of the Company and its Restricted Subsidiaries to any Unrestricted Subsidiary; non-exclusive ordinary-course licenses to an Unrestricted Subsidiary are permitted so long as the Company and its Restricted Subsidiaries retain beneficial ownership and the same use rights.
units.notes: A cross-covenant anti-trap-door provision that overrides the Section 6.02, 6.04, 6.05 and 6.08 permissions.

units.description: No Loan Party or Restricted Subsidiary may enter into any Sale and Leaseback Transaction except a sale of fixed or capital assets that is (a) made for cash consideration not less than the fair value of the asset and (b) consummated within 180 days after the asset is acquired or its construction completed; provided that Sale and Leaseback Transactions made in reliance on Sections 6.05(e)(ii) or 6.05(k) are not subject to the 180-day requirement in clause (b).
units.notes: The carve-out from clause (b) makes the Section 6.05(e)(ii) HISCO basket and the Section 6.05(k) general basket the routes for sale-leasebacks of seasoned assets.

units.description: No Loan Party or Restricted Subsidiary may enter into any Swap Agreement except (a) Swap Agreements to hedge or mitigate risks to which a Loan Party or Restricted Subsidiary has actual exposure (other than exposure in respect of its own Equity Interests) and (b) Swap Agreements to cap, collar or exchange interest rates with respect to any interest-bearing liability or investment.

Restricted Payment covenant lead-in: no Loan Party will, nor permit any Restricted Subsidiary to, declare or make, agree to make, or incur any obligation to make, directly or indirectly, any Restricted Payment except as permitted by clauses (i) through (v).

Section 6.08(a)(i) permits each Borrower may declare and pay dividends on its common stock payable solely in additional shares of common stock and, on its preferred stock, payable solely in additional shares of such preferred stock (to the extent issuable) or in common stock.
Section 6.08(a)(ii) permits Restricted Subsidiaries may declare and pay dividends ratably with respect to their Equity Interests.

Section 6.08(a)(iii) permits Loan Parties may make Restricted Payments pursuant to and in accordance with stock option plans or other benefit plans for management or employees of the Loan Parties and their Restricted Subsidiaries.

Section 6.08(a)(iv) permits other Restricted Payments in an amount not exceeding the Available Amount immediately prior to the payment, so long as at the time and after giving pro forma effect (x) no Event of Default exists or would result and (y) the Total Net Leverage Ratio is not greater than the LESSER of (A) 2.5 to 1.00 and (B) the ratio 0.5 to 1.00 lower than the maximum Total Net Leverage Ratio permitted under Section 6.12 at such time.
units.notes: Shares the Available Amount with Section 6.04(q) investments; the hard 2.5x ceiling is more restrictive than the 0.5x-cushion test used for investments.

units.description: Section 6.08(a)(v) permits the Company may make distributions and pay dividends to equityholders not otherwise permitted, up to $10,000,000 during any fiscal year, provided (x) no Default exists immediately before or after and (y) the Company is in pro forma compliance with Section 6.12 without giving effect to any Total Net Leverage Ratio Adjustment; provided that a payment made in reliance on this clause is NOT counted against the $10,000,000 limit if, after giving pro forma effect, the Total Net Leverage Ratio is not greater than the lesser of (A) 2.5 to 1.00 and (B) the ratio 0.5 to 1.00 lower than the maximum permitted under Section 6.12.
units.notes: The dollar cap is effectively unlimited at sub-2.5x leverage; note the express disregard of any Total Net Leverage Ratio Adjustment for the pro forma test.

units.description: No Loan Party will, nor permit any Restricted Subsidiary to, make or agree to make any payment or distribution of or in respect of principal or interest on any Indebtedness, or any payment on account of the purchase, redemption, retirement, acquisition, cancellation or termination of any Indebtedness, except as permitted by clauses (i) through (iv).
Section 6.08(b)(i) permits payment of Indebtedness created under the Loan Documents.

Section 6.08(b)(ii) permits payment of regularly scheduled interest and principal when due on Indebtedness permitted under Section 6.01, other than payments on Subordinated Indebtedness prohibited by its subordination provisions.
Section 6.08(b)(iii) permits refinancings of Indebtedness to the extent permitted by Section 6.01.

Section 6.08(b)(iv) permits payment of secured Indebtedness that becomes due as a result of a voluntary sale or transfer of the securing property to the extent the sale or transfer is permitted by Section 6.05.

Affiliate transaction covenant lead-in: no Loan Party will, nor permit any Restricted Subsidiary to, sell, lease or otherwise transfer property or assets to, purchase, lease or acquire property or assets from, or otherwise engage in transactions with, any Affiliate, except as permitted by clauses (a) through (g).
units.notes: Note clause (b) permits intra-U.S. and intra-Canadian Loan Party transactions but NOT cross-border Loan Party transactions, which must instead satisfy clause (a)'s arm's-length and ordinary-course tests - the mechanism Section 6.05(b) relies on.

units.description: Section 6.09(a) permits transactions that (i) are in the ordinary course of business and (ii) are at prices and on terms and conditions not less favorable to the Loan Party or Restricted Subsidiary than could be obtained on an arm's-length basis from unrelated third parties.

Section 6.09(b) permits transactions (i) between or among the U.S. Loan Parties not involving any other Affiliate and (ii) between or among the Canadian Loan Parties not involving any other Affiliate.
Section 6.09(c) permits any investment permitted by Sections 6.04(b), 6.04(c) or 6.04(d).
Section 6.09(d) permits any Indebtedness permitted under Sections 6.01(b) or 6.01(c).
Section 6.09(e) permits any Restricted Payment permitted by Section 6.08.

Section 6.09(f) permits payment of reasonable fees to non-employee directors and compensation, employee benefit arrangements and indemnities for directors, officers or employees in the ordinary course.

Section 6.09(g) permits issuances of securities or other payments, awards or grants in cash, securities or otherwise pursuant to, or the funding of, employment agreements, stock options and stock ownership plans approved by a Loan Party's board of directors.

No Loan Party or Restricted Subsidiary may enter into, incur or permit to exist any agreement prohibiting, restricting or conditioning (a) the ability to create, incur or permit Liens on its property or (b) the ability of a Restricted Subsidiary to pay dividends or distributions on Equity Interests, make or repay loans or advances to a Borrower or other Restricted Subsidiary, or Guarantee Indebtedness of a Borrower or other Restricted Subsidiary; exceptions: (i) restrictions imposed by applicable law or the Loan Documents; (ii) restrictions existing on the date of the Agreement identified on Schedule 6.10 (but not extensions, renewals or scope-expanding amendments); (iii) customary restrictions in agreements for the sale of assets or a Restricted Subsidiary pending a permitted sale, applying only to the assets or entity to be sold; (iv) as to clause (a) only, restrictions in agreements for secured Indebtedness permitted by the Agreement that apply only to the securing property; and (v) as to clause (a) only, customary anti-assignment provisions in leases and other contracts.
units.notes: Defines 'Burdensome Restrictions' for the Section 3.19 representation.

units.description: No Loan Party or Restricted Subsidiary may amend, modify or waive its rights under (a) any agreement relating to Subordinated Indebtedness, (b) any Closing Date Acquisition Document, (c) the HISCO Acquisition Agreement or (d) its organizational or governing documents, in each case to the extent the amendment, modification or waiver would be materially adverse to the Lenders.
units.notes: The Source Atlantic Share Purchase Agreement was NOT added to this list even though the Source Atlantic Acquisition was added to the Permitted Acquisition definition.

units.description: Interest Coverage Ratio covenant: the Company will not permit the Interest Coverage Ratio, for any period of four consecutive fiscal quarters ending on the last day of any fiscal quarter (commencing with the fiscal quarter ending June 30, 2022), to be less than 3.00 to 1.00.
units.notes: Unchanged level; tested quarterly with no step-downs and no Total Net Leverage Ratio Adjustment analogue.

units.description: Total Net Leverage Ratio covenant AS AMENDED: the Company will not permit the Total Net Leverage Ratio on the last day of any fiscal quarter ending on or after June 30, 2023 to exceed (i) 4.50 to 1.00 for fiscal quarters ending on or after June 30, 2023 but prior to September 30, 2024; (ii) 4.25 to 1.00 for fiscal quarters ending on or after September 30, 2024 but prior to September 30, 2025; (iii) 4.00 to 1.00 for fiscal quarters ending on or after September 30, 2025 but prior to September 30, 2026; and (iv) 3.75 to 1.00 for fiscal quarters ending on or after September 30, 2026. TOTAL NET LEVERAGE RATIO ADJUSTMENT: upon written request of the Borrower Representative in connection with a Material Acquisition, the applicable maximum ratio for each of the four fiscal quarters ending immediately after the consummation date is increased by up to 0.50 to 1.00 as requested in writing by the Company, provided that the adjustment may be used (i) only twice during the term of the Agreement AFTER THE THIRD AMENDMENT EFFECTIVE DATE - and, at the Company's option, the adjustment may be applied to the Source Atlantic Acquisition WITHOUT reducing the availability of the two permitted uses - and (ii) only if no Event of Default has occurred and is continuing; and provided further that the Total Net Leverage Ratio may never be increased above 4.50 to 1.00 as a result of an adjustment. On notice of an election, the Administrative Agent notifies the Lenders and the Agreement is automatically amended to reflect the adjustment.
units.notes: Two Third Amendment changes here: the usage counter is reset to run from the Third Amendment Effective Date (previously the First Amendment Effective Date), and the Source Atlantic Acquisition adjustment is free of charge. Because the current level (until September 30, 2024) is already 4.50x, the 4.50x hard ceiling means no adjustment headroom exists in that window.

articles.heading: Events of Default (as amended and restated)

units.description: Events of Default as restated, clauses (a) through (q): (a) failure to pay principal of any Loan or any LC reimbursement obligation when due (no grace); (b) failure to pay interest, fees or other amounts, continuing for three Business Days; (c) any representation or warranty proving incorrect in any material respect when made or deemed made; (d) failure to observe or perform Section 5.02(a) (Default notices), Section 5.03 (Loan Party existence), Section 5.08 (use of proceeds), Section 5.14 (post-closing) or ANY provision of Article VI - with no cure period; (e) failure to perform any other covenant, with a 5-day cure (after knowledge or notice) for Sections 5.01, 5.02 (other than 5.02(a)), 5.06 and 5.13, and a 30-day cure for all other provisions of the Agreement or any other Loan Document; (f) failure to pay Material Indebtedness when due; (g) any event causing Material Indebtedness to become due, or permitting holders to accelerate or require prepayment, prior to scheduled maturity (excluding secured debt becoming due on a voluntary sale permitted by Section 6.05); (h) involuntary insolvency proceedings under any Insolvency Law undismissed for 60 days, or entry of an approving order; (i) voluntary insolvency proceedings, consent to involuntary proceedings, application for or consent to a receiver or similar official, admission of allegations, general assignment for creditors, or any action to effect the foregoing; (j) inability, written admission of inability or public declaration of intent not to pay debts as they become due, or a Canadian Loan Party becoming an 'insolvent person' under the Bankruptcy and Insolvency Act (Canada); (k) money judgments exceeding $20,000,000 in the aggregate (net of insurance where the insurer has been notified and has not denied coverage) undischarged for 60 consecutive days without effective stay, any judgment creditor attachment or levy, or failure within 60 days to discharge non-monetary judgments that could reasonably be expected to have a Material Adverse Effect; (l) an ERISA Event or Canadian Pension Event that, in the Required Lenders' opinion and together with all others, could reasonably be expected to result in aggregate liability exceeding $20,000,000; (m) a Change in Control; (n) the Loan Guaranty ceasing to be in full force, any action to discontinue or assert its invalidity, any Loan Guarantor failing to comply with or denying liability under it; (o) any Collateral Document failing to create a valid security interest or any Lien securing a Secured Obligation ceasing to be a perfected first priority Lien (other than Permitted Liens); (p) any Collateral Document ceasing to be in full force or any action to assert its invalidity; and (q) any material provision of any Loan Document ceasing to be valid, binding and enforceable, or any Loan Party challenging or asserting its unenforceability.
units.notes: Clause (d)'s no-grace treatment of every Article VI covenant is what makes each basket-level analysis in Article VI immediately consequential.

units.description: (a) On any Event of Default other than a Section 7.01(h)/(i) Borrower insolvency event, the Administrative Agent may, and at Required Lender request must, on notice to the Borrower Representative (i) terminate the Commitments (including the Swingline Commitment), (ii) declare the Loans due and payable in whole or ratably in part together with accrued interest, all fees (including break funding payments) and other Secured Obligations, without presentment or demand, (iii) require 103% cash collateral for LC Exposure under Section 2.06(j), and (iv) exercise all rights and remedies under the Loan Documents and applicable law; for Section 7.01(h)/(i) Borrower insolvency events, Commitments terminate and all Loans, LC cash collateral, interest, fees and Secured Obligations become due automatically. Default interest may also be imposed. (b) The Administrative Agent may exercise all UCC/PPSA secured party remedies, including collection, appropriation, credit bidding, public or private sale (with the right to purchase free of any equity of redemption), assembly of Collateral, and application of net proceeds after costs to the obligations in such order as it elects, accounting for any surplus only after payment of amounts required by law; 10 days' notice of a proposed sale is deemed reasonable.

Equity Cure: (a) for purposes of determining whether a Default or Event of Default under Section 6.12 has occurred for any fiscal quarter, until the tenth Business Day after financial statements for that quarter are required to be delivered (the 'Cure Expiration Date'), the Company may issue Qualified Stock and apply the net cash proceeds (a 'Specified Equity Contribution') to increase EBITDA for that quarter, provided the proceeds are actually received as cash common equity by the Cure Expiration Date, are Not Otherwise Applied, and are notified to the Administrative Agent on receipt (with the designated amount permitted to be reduced to the amount needed). (b) Conditions: no more than two Specified Equity Contributions in any four consecutive fiscal quarters; no more than five in the aggregate during the term; the amount may not exceed what is required for pro forma Section 6.12 compliance; no pro forma reduction in Indebtedness (including netting) is permitted for the cured quarter; Specified Equity Contributions count only for Section 6.12 compliance and are disregarded for pricing, other financial-covenant or ratio-based conditions (including pro forma basket tests), the Available Amount and all other purposes; and after notice of an intent to cure, no Loans need be made and no Letters of Credit issued, amended or extended until the contribution is made. (c) On receipt of the proceeds before the Cure Expiration Date the Section 6.12 covenants are deemed satisfied for that quarter and any related Default is deemed not to have occurred; and after a notice of intent to cure, neither the Administrative Agent nor any Lender may exercise remedies based solely on a Section 6.12 failure until the failure is not cured by the Cure Expiration Date.
units.notes: The express exclusion of Specified Equity Contributions from the Available Amount and from pro forma basket tests prevents an equity cure from also creating covenant capacity.

articles.heading: The Administrative Agent (as amended and restated)

units.description: Authorization and Action - irrevocable appointment of JPMorgan as administrative agent and collateral agent, grant of powers of attorney for non-U.S. Collateral Documents, duty to act only on Required Lender instructions (with indemnity and illegality/automatic stay protections), express disclaimer of fiduciary or trustee duties (including under Canadian law), no duty to disclose information, no obligation to expend its own funds, permitted use of sub-agents and Related Parties, disclaimer of Arranger duties, authority to file claims in insolvency proceedings without authority to vote on plans, and confirmation that Article VIII is solely for the benefit of the Agent, Lenders and Issuing Banks.

Administrative Agent's Reliance, Indemnification, Etc. - exculpation for actions taken with Required Lender consent or absent gross negligence or willful misconduct, no responsibility for Loan Party representations or document sufficiency, deemed lack of knowledge of Section 5.02 notices and Defaults absent express written notice, no duty to ascertain compliance, perfection, priority or Affiliate Lender compliance, no liability for Revolving Exposure, Exchange Rate or Dollar Equivalent determinations, and permitted reliance on the Register, counsel, experts and apparently genuine communications; plus an express disclaimer of any duty to monitor or enforce the Disqualified Institution provisions.

Posting of Communications - the Administrative Agent may post Communications on an Approved Electronic Platform; the platform and Communications are provided 'as is' and 'as available' with a full disclaimer of warranties and of Applicable Party liability for damages; notice that Communications have been posted constitutes effective delivery; Lenders must supply email addresses; the Agent may store Communications per its retention policies; other notice methods are preserved.

The Administrative Agent Individually - JPMorgan has the same rights and obligations as any other Lender or Issuing Bank in respect of its Commitment, Loans and Letters of Credit, is included in 'Lenders'/'Required Lenders' definitions, and may engage in any banking or other business with any Loan Party without accounting to the Lenders.

Successor Administrative Agent - resignation on 30 days' notice, Required Lender appointment of a successor (subject to Borrower Representative approval not unreasonably withheld and not required during a continuing Event of Default), fallback appointment by the retiring Agent, and, if no successor accepts within 30 days, discharge of the retiring Agent with the Required Lenders succeeding to its rights and duties while the retiring Agent continues to hold security interests and possessory Collateral as collateral agent; survival of exculpation, reimbursement and indemnification provisions.

Acknowledgements of Lenders and Issuing Banks - Lender representations that this is a commercial lending facility and that each made its own credit decision; deemed consent to Effective Date deliverables; a full erroneous-payment regime requiring return of erroneous Payments within one Business Day with interest, waiver of discharge-for-value defenses, notice obligations on off-pattern Payments, Administrative Agent subrogation, confirmation that erroneous Payments do not discharge Obligations, and survival; and Lender acknowledgements regarding Reports (no representation as to accuracy, confidentiality, and indemnification of the Agent and preparers).

Collateral Matters - no Secured Party may individually realize on Collateral or enforce Guarantees (other than setoff under Section 9.08 or filing proofs of claim); the Administrative Agent is the 'representative' of the Secured Parties under the UCC and is granted a power of attorney to perfect additional Collateral; Banking Services and Swap Agreement providers get no Collateral management or release rights and are deemed to appoint the Agent and be bound as Secured Parties; the Agent has no duty to ascertain the existence, value, collectability, priority or perfection of Collateral or to monitor or maintain it.

Credit Bidding - the Secured Parties irrevocably authorize the Administrative Agent, at Required Lender direction, to credit bid all or any portion of the Secured Obligations and purchase Collateral (directly or through acquisition vehicles) at Bankruptcy Code Sections 363/1123/1129 sales, foreclosures or deeds in lieu, with ratable credit bidding, deemed assignment of ratable interests to acquisition vehicles, Required Lender control of governance, issuance of interests or debt instruments to Secured Parties, and automatic reassignment and cancellation if the bid is unsuccessful.

Certain ERISA Matters - each Lender represents and covenants that at least one of four alternatives is true (no Benefit Plan 'plan assets'; a PTE exemption such as PTE 84-14, 95-60, 90-1, 91-38 or 96-23 applies; the QPAM conditions of PTE 84-14 are satisfied; or another agreed representation), and, unless the first alternative applies, that none of the Administrative Agent or Arrangers is a fiduciary; the Agent and Arrangers disclaim investment advice and disclose their financial interests.

Flood Laws - JPMorgan will post flood-related documents received to the applicable electronic platform but each federally regulated Lender or Participant remains responsible for its own compliance with the National Flood Insurance Reform Act of 1994 and related legislation.

Quebec Security - each Lender appoints the Administrative Agent as hypothecary representative under article 2692 of the Civil Code of Quebec to hold any Quebec hypothec securing the Obligations, with the same rights, powers, immunities and indemnities as the Administrative Agent generally; successors and new Lenders are deemed to ratify the appointment.

Borrower Communications (a NEWLY ADDED Section in the restated agreement) - the Borrowers may deliver Borrower Communications (Borrowing Requests, Interest Election Requests, prepayment notices, LC issuance/amendment/extension requests and other notices and documents) to the Administrative Agent through an 'Approved Borrower Portal' chosen by the Administrative Agent, subject to approved procedures; the parties acknowledge that electronic distribution is not necessarily secure, that the Agent is not responsible for vetting Borrower administrators or contacts, and that confidentiality and other risks exist; the portal is provided 'as is' and 'as available' with a full warranty disclaimer and exclusion of Applicable Party liability; the Agent may store Borrower Communications per its retention policies; and other notice methods remain available.

Notice provisions AS AMENDED. Loan Party notices go to the Borrower Representative at Distribution Solutions Group, Inc., 8770 W. Bryn Mawr Ave., Suite 900, Chicago, IL 60631, Attention: Ron Knutson, Chief Financial Officer, with a courtesy copy to Mayer Brown LLP (Attn: Fred Fisher). Administrative Agent, Swingline Lender, Issuing Bank and collateral agent notices go to JPMorgan Chase Bank, N.A., 131 S Dearborn St, Floor 04, Chicago, IL 60603-5506, with named attention lines and with the prior specific email addresses replaced by contact details 'On File with the Borrower Representative and the Lenders'; specialized addresses remain for agency withholding tax inquiries, covenant compliance and DQ List notifications. Other Lenders and Issuing Banks are noticed at their Administrative Questionnaire addresses. Delivery rules distinguish hand/courier/mail (on receipt), fax (when sent, with next-business-day deeming outside business hours) and Electronic Systems/Approved Electronic Platforms; Article II notices and Section 5.01(c) compliance certificates are excluded from electronic delivery unless otherwise provided or agreed. Any party may change its address by notice.
