units.description: (a) No failure or delay operates as a waiver; rights are cumulative; waivers are effective only as permitted by paragraph (b) and only for the specific instance. (b) Subject to Section 2.09 (Incremental Facility Amendments and Commitment Schedule modifications) and Sections 2.14(b)/(c) and 9.02(c)/(e), amendments require the Borrowers and Required Lenders (or, for other Loan Documents, the Administrative Agent and the relevant Loan Parties with Required Lender consent), provided that: (A) increasing a Lender's Commitment requires that Lender's consent; (B) reducing or forgiving principal, LC Disbursements, interest rate, interest or fees requires each directly affected Lender's consent (amendments to the financial covenants or the defined terms used in them are expressly NOT interest or fee reductions); (C) postponing any scheduled payment date, reducing or waiving any payment or postponing any Commitment expiration requires each directly affected Lender's consent (other than Section 2.11(c) mandatory prepayments); (D) changing Section 2.09(d) or Section 2.18(b)/(d) so as to alter ratable Commitment reductions or the payment waterfall or sharing requires each Lender's consent; (E) changing this Section, the 'Required Lenders' definition or any voting threshold requires each directly affected Lender's consent (with Incremental Term Loans and additional Revolving Commitments includable in Required Lender determinations solely with Section 2.09 parties' consent); (F) changing Section 2.20 requires each Lender's consent; (G) releasing any Guarantor from the Loan Guaranty requires each Lender's consent; (H) releasing all or substantially all Collateral requires each Lender's consent; and (I) changing the 'Alternative Currency' definition requires each Revolving Lender's consent - in each case excluding Defaulting Lenders and Affiliate Lenders where indicated; plus Administrative Agent, Swingline Lender and Issuing Bank consent rights and a Class-specific amendment mechanism. (c) Lender authorization for the Administrative Agent to release Liens on Payment in Full, on permitted dispositions (including release of a Restricted Subsidiary's Loan Guaranty where 100% of its Equity Interests are sold), on expired leases and in remedies exercises, with discretionary annual releases up to $500,000 of Collateral value and releases in connection with permitted transactions, and authorization to subordinate or release Liens to accommodate permitted purchase money financings. (d) Non-Consenting Lender replacement mechanism, including payment of Section 2.16-equivalent amounts. (e) The Administrative Agent may, with only the Borrower Representative's consent, amend the Loan Documents to cure ambiguities, omissions, mistakes, defects or inconsistencies.
units.notes: The express carve-out in clause (B) - that amendments to financial covenants or their defined terms are not interest/fee reductions - is what allowed the Section 6.12 and definitional changes here to pass on a Required Lender vote.

units.description: Expenses; Indemnity; Damage Waiver - the Loan Parties jointly and severally pay reasonable and documented out-of-pocket syndication, administration, amendment and waiver expenses (limited to one counsel per jurisdiction plus conflict counsel), Issuing Bank LC expenses, and enforcement/workout expenses; enumerated reimbursable items include appraisals and insurance reviews, field examinations and Reports, lien searches and filings, sums advanced to cure Loan Party failures, and collection/lockbox costs, several of which are available only during a continuing Event of Default. The Loan Parties indemnify each Indemnitee for Liabilities and related expenses arising from the Loan Documents, the Transactions, any Loan or Letter of Credit or use of proceeds, Hazardous Materials or Environmental Liability, the Agent's administration and related Proceedings, excluding matters resulting from the Indemnitee's gross negligence, willful misconduct or bad faith or from disputes solely among Indemnitees; Lenders severally backstop the Loan Parties' obligations to Agent Indemnitees ratably by Applicable Percentage. Loan Parties waive claims for information-transmission Liabilities and for special, indirect, consequential and punitive damages against any Lender-Related Person. Amounts are payable promptly after written demand.

Survival - all covenants, agreements, representations and warranties survive execution, the making of Loans and issuance of Letters of Credit and continue until Payment in Full, regardless of investigation or notice of any Default; Sections 2.15, 2.16, 2.17 and 9.03 and Article VIII survive termination and repayment.

Counterparts; Integration; Effectiveness; Electronic Execution - counterpart execution; the Agreement, other Loan Documents and separate fee and Issuing Bank Sublimit letters constitute the entire contract; effectiveness on receipt of counterparts subject to Section 4.01; and an extensive Electronic Signature and Ancillary Document regime giving electronic signatures and imaged records the same effect as manually executed paper originals, subject to the Administrative Agent's right to require manual counterparts, with related waivers.
Severability - invalid provisions are ineffective only to the extent of the invalidity and only in the relevant jurisdiction.

Right of Setoff - upon a continuing Event of Default each Lender, Issuing Bank and their Affiliates may set off deposits and other obligations against Secured Obligations, whether or not demand has been made and whether or not the obligations are contingent, unmatured or booked at a different office; a Defaulting Lender's setoff proceeds must be paid over to the Administrative Agent for Section 2.20 application and segregated in trust in the interim; notice failures do not affect validity.

Governing Law; Jurisdiction; Consent to Service of Process - Illinois internal law governs (giving effect to federal laws applicable to national banks); claims against the Administrative Agent by Secured Parties are governed by Illinois law notwithstanding other Loan Document choices; exclusive jurisdiction in U.S. federal or Illinois state courts sitting in Chicago (with claims against the Agent and its Related Parties maintainable only there); venue and forum non conveniens waivers; consent to service as provided in Section 9.01, with each Canadian Loan Party irrevocably appointing the Borrower Representative as its agent for service until Payment in Full and waiving sovereign-style immunity.

WAIVER OF JURY TRIAL - each party waives, to the fullest extent permitted, any right to trial by jury in any proceeding arising out of or relating to the Agreement, any other Loan Document or the transactions contemplated, with the customary certifications and acknowledgements.
Headings - Article and Section headings and the Table of Contents are for convenience only and do not affect construction.

Confidentiality - the Administrative Agent, Issuing Bank and Lenders maintain the confidentiality of Information, with nine enumerated permitted disclosures including to affiliates and advisors, Governmental Authorities and self-regulatory bodies, as required by law or legal process, to other parties, in remedies or enforcement, to assignees/Participants and prospective assignees/Participants (including disclosure of the DQ List), to swap counterparties and to insurers/reinsurers providing credit risk mitigation, with Borrower Representative consent, to rating agencies and the CUSIP Service Bureau, and where the Information becomes public other than by breach or is obtained from another source; 'Information' excludes pre-disclosure non-confidential information and league-table data; plus all-caps material non-public information acknowledgements by each Lender.

Several Obligations; Nonreliance; Violation of Law - Lender obligations are several; each Lender represents it is not relying on margin stock for repayment; no Lender or Issuing Bank is obligated to extend credit in violation of any Requirement of Law.
USA PATRIOT Act - each subject Lender notifies each Loan Party of its obligation to obtain, verify and record identifying information.
Disclosure - acknowledgement that the Administrative Agent and its Affiliates may hold investments in, lend to, or have other relationships with the Loan Parties and their Affiliates.

Appointment for Perfection - each Lender appoints each other Lender as its agent to perfect Liens requiring possession or control, with an obligation to notify and deliver Collateral to the Administrative Agent on request.

Interest Rate Limitation - if the interest rate plus Charges on any Loan would exceed the Maximum Rate, the rate is limited to the Maximum Rate and the excess is cumulated and recovered from later interest and Charges (not above the Maximum Rate) plus interest at the Overnight Rate.

No Fiduciary Duty, etc. - each Credit Party acts solely as an arm's-length contractual counterparty and not as advisor, fiduciary or agent; no claims may be asserted for breach of fiduciary duty; disclosures regarding full-service securities and banking activities, potential conflicting relationships and the non-use of confidential information for other clients.

Marketing Consent - the Borrowers authorize JPMorgan and its affiliates, at their expense and to the extent approved by the Borrower Representative (approval not unreasonably withheld, conditioned or delayed), to use the Borrowers' name and logo in advertising and to publicize the Agreement, revocable by written notice.

Acknowledgement and Consent to Bail-In of Affected Financial Institutions - each party consents to the exercise of Write-Down and Conversion Powers by the applicable Resolution Authority over liabilities of Affected Financial Institutions, including reduction, cancellation, conversion into equity instruments and variation of terms.

Acknowledgement Regarding Any Supported QFCs - for QFC Credit Support, transfers of Supported QFCs and QFC Credit Support from a Covered Party in a U.S. Special Resolution Regime proceeding are effective as they would be under U.S. law, and Default Rights are exercisable only to the extent permitted under those regimes, with defined terms Covered Entity, Default Right and QFC.

Canadian Anti-Money Laundering Legislation - Loan Parties will promptly provide CAML information regarding themselves, their directors, signing officers and controlling persons; the Administrative Agent has no obligation to ascertain identity on any Lender's behalf.

Judgment Currency - conversion for judgment purposes uses the Administrative Agent's normal-procedure purchase rate on the Business Day preceding judgment; obligations are discharged only to the extent dollars can be purchased on the Business Day after receipt, with indemnity for shortfalls and remittance of excess.

Successors and Assigns as restated: (a) no Borrower may assign without each Lender's consent; no Lender may assign except under this Section; limited third-party beneficiaries. (b) Assignments require the consent (not unreasonably withheld) of the Borrower Representative (deemed given if not objected to within ten Business Days; not required for assignments to a Lender, a Lender Affiliate (other than a Defaulting Lender), an Approved Fund or, during a continuing Event of Default, any assignee), the Administrative Agent (not required for revolving assignments to an existing Revolving Lender or for Term Loan assignments to a Lender, Lender Affiliate or Approved Fund), the Issuing Bank and the Swingline Lender (neither required for Term Loan assignments); with minimum assignment amounts of $5,000,000 (revolving) and $1,000,000 (term) except for assignments to Lenders, Lender Affiliates, Approved Funds or of an entire remaining position, proportionate-part requirements, a $3,500 processing fee, Administrative Questionnaire delivery, and defined terms 'Approved Fund' and 'Ineligible Institution' (natural persons; a Defaulting Lender or its Parent; personal holding vehicles subject to a three-part professional-management/$25,000,000 asset exception; during a continuing Event of Default any non-Lender that would hold more than 25% of Aggregate Revolving Exposure or Commitments; Loan Parties and their Subsidiaries and Affiliates except as permitted by Sections 9.04(f) and (g); and Disqualified Institutions); with Register maintenance and recordation provisions. (c) Participations may be sold without consent to non-Ineligible Institutions, with the Lender retaining enforcement and voting rights except for first-proviso Section 9.02(b) matters affecting the Participant, Participant entitlement to Sections 2.15, 2.16 and 2.17 subject to the no-greater-payment limitation, and a Participant Register requirement. (d) Pledges to Federal Reserve Banks are permitted without release of obligations. (e) Disqualified Institution regime: no assignment or participation to a Person that was a Disqualified Institution on the Trade Date without Company consent, non-retroactive treatment of later-designated Disqualified Institutions, Company right to force assignment at the lesser of par and the acquisition price, deprivation of information, meeting and platform access rights, deemed proportionate voting, plan-of-reorganization voting restrictions and designation under Bankruptcy Code Section 1126(e), and Administrative Agent authority to post the DQ List. (f) Affiliate Lender regime: assignments of Term Loans to Affiliate Lenders (including Debt Fund Affiliates) only through a Dutch Auction or non-pro rata open market purchase per agreed procedures, with no continuing Event of Default under Sections 7.01(a), (b), (h) or (i), an Affiliate Lender Assignment and Assumption in the form of Exhibit F, a 20% Affiliate Lender Cap (excluding Debt Fund Affiliates) on Term Loans and Incremental Term Loans, deemed proportionate plan voting by the Administrative Agent (subject to disproportionate-treatment protections), disclosure and status affirmation requirements, exclusion from lender-only meetings and information, MNPI representations or disclosure, and a prohibition on using Loan proceeds to fund the purchase; Affiliate Lenders may contribute purchased Term Loans to the Borrowers for cancellation with pro rata reduction of amortization; and voting rules deem Affiliate Lender Term Loans voted proportionately, cap Debt Fund Affiliates at 25% of Required Lender calculations, preserve each-Lender and directly-affected voting rights, and protect against disproportionate treatment. (g) Loan Buyback regime: the Company, any Borrower or Restricted Subsidiary may purchase Term Loans only through a Dutch Auction or non-pro rata open market purchases not exceeding $20,000,000 in the aggregate, with no continuing Event of Default, automatic and permanent cancellation on acquisition, no use of Loan proceeds, pro rata reduction of the Class principal and amortization, MNPI representations or disclosure, and confirmation that such purchases are not prepayments.
units.notes: The 20% Affiliate Lender Cap, the 25% Debt Fund Affiliate voting cap and the $20,000,000 open-market buyback limit are hard numerical constraints that interact with the Required Lenders definition.

units.description: (a) Each U.S. Loan Guarantor is jointly and severally liable for, and as primary obligor absolutely, unconditionally and irrevocably guarantees, prompt payment of the Secured Obligations plus Section 9.03 collection costs (the 'U.S. Guaranteed Obligations'), excluding Excluded Swap Obligations of that guarantor; extensions and renewals do not release it, and the guaranty is enforceable by any branch or Affiliate of any Lender. (b) Each Canadian Loan Guarantor similarly guarantees the CANADIAN Secured Obligations plus collection costs (the 'Canadian Guaranteed Obligations'), excluding its Excluded Swap Obligations, and it is expressly provided that NO CANADIAN LOAN PARTY GUARANTEES ANY U.S. SECURED OBLIGATIONS.
units.notes: The single most important entity-applicability rule in the structure: Canadian credit support runs only to Canadian Secured Obligations.

units.description: Guaranty of Payment - the Loan Guaranty is a guaranty of payment and not of collection; each Loan Guarantor waives any right to require suit against a Borrower, another Loan Guarantor or any Obligated Party or enforcement against collateral first.

No Discharge or Diminishment of Loan Guaranty - guarantor obligations are unconditional and absolute and not subject to reduction, limitation, impairment or termination for any reason other than Payment in Full, including waivers, releases, settlements, changes in Borrower structure or ownership, insolvency proceedings and resulting discharges, or guarantor claims and setoffs; no defense, setoff, counterclaim or recoupment based on invalidity, illegality or unenforceability; and no discharge from failure to assert claims, waivers or modifications, release or invalidity of security, agent inaction as to collateral, or payment defaults or delays.

Defenses Waived - waiver of defenses based on Borrower or guarantor defenses, unenforceability or cessation of liability other than Payment in Full; waiver of acceptance, presentment, demand, protest and unspecified notices and of any requirement of prior action against an Obligated Party; confirmation of non-surety status; and waiver of election-of-remedies defenses arising from judicial or non-judicial foreclosure, deed in lieu, compromise or other accommodations even where they impair subrogation or reimbursement rights.

Rights of Subrogation - no Loan Guarantor may assert subrogation, contribution or indemnification claims against any Obligated Party or collateral until the Loan Parties and Loan Guarantors have fully performed all obligations to the Administrative Agent, Issuing Bank and Lenders.

Reinstatement; Stay of Acceleration - guaranty obligations are reinstated if any payment is rescinded, restored or returned on insolvency or otherwise; if acceleration is stayed by insolvency, the guaranteed amounts are nonetheless payable on demand.
Information - each Loan Guarantor assumes responsibility for informing itself of the Borrowers' condition and the risks it assumes; no Credit Party has a duty to advise it.

Release of Loan Guarantors - (a) a Loan Guarantor (other than a Borrower) is automatically released upon a permitted transaction in which it ceases to be a Restricted Subsidiary, PROVIDED (language added in the restated version) that the transaction was not entered into for the purpose of causing the Person not to be a Loan Guarantor, and provided further that, if required by the Agreement, the Required Lenders consented and their consent did not provide otherwise; the Administrative Agent executes release documentation on request without recourse or warranty. (b) The Administrative Agent may, at the Company's request, release any Loan Guarantor (other than a Borrower) that is no longer a Material Subsidiary. (c) On Payment in Full the Loan Guaranty terminates automatically.
Taxes - guaranty payments are made without withholding unless required by law, with timely payment of withheld amounts and gross-up for Indemnified Taxes.

Maximum Liability - each Loan Guarantor's guaranteed amount is limited as necessary to avoid avoidance under Bankruptcy Code Section 548 or applicable fraudulent transfer statutes or common law, taking into account subrogation, indemnification and contribution rights.

Contribution - a Loan Guarantor making a Guarantor Payment exceeding its 'Allocable Amount' share is entitled, after indefeasible payment in full and Payment in Full of the Guaranteed Obligations and termination of the Agreement, to contribution and indemnification from the other Loan Guarantors pro rata by Allocable Amounts (fair saleable value of property over total liabilities, giving effect to other guarantors' ratable shares of contingent liabilities); the section defines relative rights only, does not impair joint and several liability, creates assets of the paying guarantors and is exercisable only upon Payment in Full.

Liability Cumulative - each Loan Party's liability as Loan Guarantor is in addition to and cumulative with all its other liabilities under the Loan Documents, without limitation as to amount unless expressly provided otherwise.

Keepwell - each Qualified ECP Guarantor jointly and severally undertakes to provide funds or other support needed by each other Guarantor to honor its Swap Obligation guarantee obligations, limited to the maximum amount that would not render the undertaking voidable under fraudulent conveyance law, effective until all Swap Obligations terminate, and intended to constitute a keepwell under Commodity Exchange Act Section 1a(18)(A)(v)(II).

articles.heading: The Borrower Representative (as amended and restated)

units.description: Appointment; Nature of Relationship - the Company is appointed by each Borrower as contractual representative (the 'Borrower Representative') under the Agreement and the other Loan Documents, and as agent to receive all Loan proceeds in the Funding Account for prompt disbursement to the appropriate Borrowers (Revolving Loan disbursements limited to Availability); no Credit Party is liable for actions taken or omitted by the Borrower Representative or the Borrowers.

Powers - the Borrower Representative has only the powers specifically delegated plus reasonably incidental powers, with no implied duties to the Borrowers and no obligation to the Lenders except as specifically provided.
Employment of Agents - the Borrower Representative may act through authorized officers.

Notices - each Borrower must immediately notify the Borrower Representative of any Default or Event of Default in a designated 'notice of default'; the Borrower Representative must give prompt notice to the Administrative Agent and Lenders; notice to the Borrower Representative constitutes notice to each Borrower on receipt.

Successor Borrower Representative - the Borrower Representative may resign with the Administrative Agent's prior written consent, effective on appointment of a successor, with prompt written notice to the Lenders.

Execution of Loan Documents - the Borrowers empower the Borrower Representative to execute and deliver Loan Documents and related agreements, certificates, documents and instruments (including Compliance Certificates) on their behalf, and agree that its actions bind all Borrowers.

Nature and Extent of Each Borrower's Liability - (a) each U.S. Borrower is jointly and severally liable for all Secured Obligations and is a guarantor of each other Borrower's obligations; each Canadian Borrower is jointly and severally liable ONLY for the Canadian Secured Obligations and is a guarantor only of the other Canadian Borrowers' obligations, and expressly not for U.S. Secured Obligations; (b) direct liability of each Borrower for Loans made directly or indirectly to it, LC Exposure supporting its business and related interest, fees and expenses is preserved.

articles.heading: Collateral Allocation Mechanism (as amended and restated)

units.description: Collateral Allocation Mechanism: (a) on the CAM Exchange Date (the first date of a Section 7.01(h)/(i) event as to any Borrower or acceleration under Section 7.02), the Revolving Commitments automatically terminate, the principal of each Alternative Currency Revolving Loan automatically converts into Dollars at the CAM Exchange Date Exchange Rates (with all subsequent accruals and payments in Dollars at the otherwise applicable rates), and the Revolving Lenders are automatically deemed to have made reciprocal purchases so that each owns its CAM Percentage of each Designated Obligation; each Revolving Lender, each participant and each Borrower consents to the CAM Exchange and agrees to execute confirming notes and documents (failure to do so does not affect the exchange's validity). (b) After the CAM Exchange Date, payments in respect of Designated Obligations are distributed to Revolving Lenders pro rata by CAM Percentage. (c) Partial assignments of Designated Obligations after the CAM Exchange are permitted if the assignor and assignee agree on reciprocal rights in the event of a redetermination of CAM Percentages.
units.notes: Applies only to Revolving Lenders and Designated Obligations (Revolving Loan principal/interest and commitment fees), not to the Term facilities.

STRUCTURE. The Third Amendment itself is short (Sections 1-8 plus signature pages, an omitted Schedule I and a form solvency certificate as Exhibit B). Essentially all of the ~740,000 characters are Exhibit A, which is a COMPLETE marked copy of the Amended and Restated Credit Agreement dated April 1, 2022 (as previously amended by the First Amendment dated June 8, 2023 and the Second Amendment dated June 13, 2024), showing the Third Amendment's changes. Section 2(b) makes that marked copy operative, so as of August 14, 2024 the operative version of EVERY provision of Articles I-XII is the Exhibit A text. All Exhibits and Schedules other than the Commitment Schedule expressly remain in the form most recently delivered and are NOT restated here (Schedules 1.01, 3.05, 3.06, 3.10(b), 3.13, 3.14, 5.14, 6.01, 6.02, 6.04, 6.05 and 6.10 are referenced but their contents are not ascertainable from this document). 

EXTRACTION CAVEAT. The filed document uses strikethrough for deleted text and double-underline for added text. The HTML-stripped plain text preserves BOTH, without markers, so deleted language survives inline next to its replacement (e.g. 'incurred after the First Third Amendment Effective Date does not exceed $ 200,000,000 300,000,000', 'The initial As of the Third Amendment Effective Date, the aggregate amount ... is $ 200,000,000 255,000,000'). Where such doubled text appears I read the second (new) value as operative. Conversely, pure INSERTIONS are indistinguishable from unchanged text, so for a handful of provisions I could not determine from this document alone whether the change was made by the First, Second or Third Amendment; in those cases I captured the provision as amended without attributing it to a particular amendment. 

WHAT THE THIRD AMENDMENT ACTUALLY CHANGES (identifiable from surviving struck text and new defined terms): $200,000,000 of new Third Amendment Incremental Term Loans (new Section 2.01(e), amortizing $2,500,000 per quarter from December 31, 2024, maturing April 1, 2027) and a $55,000,000 revolver increase taking aggregate Revolving Commitments from $200,000,000 to $255,000,000; a two-step change to the incremental facility cap in Section 2.09(e)(ii) (temporary lift to $255,000,000 under Section 2(a) of the Amendment, then reset to $300,000,000 measured from the Third Amendment Effective Date under the restated text); conforming additions of the new tranche throughout the Applicable Percentage, Arranger, Class, Maturity Date, Term Lender/Term Loan/Term Loan Commitment, 2.07, 2.09(a), 2.09(g) (including the 50 bp MFN), 2.10(b) and 5.08 provisions; addition of the Source Atlantic Acquisition as a named Permitted Acquisition and a free-of-charge Total Net Leverage Ratio Adjustment for it in Section 6.12(b), together with a reset of the two-use Adjustment counter to run from the Third Amendment Effective Date rather than the First Amendment Effective Date; replacement of specific JPMorgan notice contacts in Section 9.01 with 'On File with the Borrower Representative and the Lenders'; and an added anti-avoidance proviso in the Section 10.08(a) guarantor release. 

CROSS-REFERENCES I HAD TO REASON ABOUT. (1) The Section 6.12(b) leverage step-down grid (4.50x / 4.25x / 4.00x / 3.75x) and the $50,000,000 Unrestricted Cash netting cap appear without struck predecessors in this document, so on this record they were set by an earlier amendment and merely carried forward; they are nonetheless the operative levels as of this Amendment. (2) The Section 6.12(b) Adjustment has a hard 4.50x ceiling, which means that while the 4.50x level is in effect (quarters ending before September 30, 2024) an Adjustment provides no headroom. (3) The Amendment's own Section 4(d) tests pro forma Section 6.12 compliance assuming the full $200,000,000 term loan AND the full $55,000,000 revolver increase are drawn - a stricter test than ordinary incurrence. (4) Section 4.02 of the restated agreement carves out only First Amendment Incremental Term Loans from the ordinary credit-event conditions; the Third Amendment Incremental Term Loans were instead conditioned solely on Section 4 of this Amendment. (5) Section 1.06 disregards any Total Net Leverage Ratio Adjustment for pro forma tests EXCEPT when testing Permitted Acquisition conditions. (6) Section 6.04(b) is drafted against '15% of EBITDA' while its two companion legs in Sections 6.01(b)(iii) and 6.01(c)(iii) are drafted against '15% of Applicable EBITDA' even though the three share a single cap - flagged, not reconciled. (7) The Source Atlantic Share Purchase Agreement was added to the Permitted Acquisition definition but was NOT added to the Section 6.11 list of Material Documents. (8) Schedule I to the Amendment (lender-level allocations) is omitted from the filing under Item 601(a)(5) of Regulation S-K, so no lender-level conclusion is supportable.
